Solana is four days away from matching a record last seen in 2022. SOL has lost 25.7% in November so far (as of Nov. 26). That's likely to become the cryptocurrency's ninth losing month this year. If December also ends in the red, that would bring the total to 10, the highest number of losing months in a single year in SOL's history.

In terms of percentage losses, 2022 was overwhelmingly the worst year for Solana. SOL lost 94.15% in 2022. So far in 2026, it's down 43.09%.

SOL declined every month between January and July. August brought a 41.5% surge, followed by another 14.56% gain in September. Then, October and November erased all those gains.

As of Nov. 26, Bitcoin had fallen roughly 21% in November. That provides some context. In October, BTC dropped 7.32%, while SOL lost 19%. Solana was already underperforming Bitcoin before November's losses accelerated.

Meanwhile, another source of demand is faltering. U.S. spot Solana ETFs have recorded $164 million in net outflows over the 30 trading days leading up to Nov. 25.

On Nov. 6, investors withdrew about $24 million from these funds. By Nov. 25, when SOL was trading around $70, the funds recorded zero net inflows. Lower prices had not yet brought ETF investors back in significant numbers.

Solana's network activity actually grew during the summer rally. Quarterly trading volume on decentralized exchanges (DEXs) increased 23% from the previous quarter to $197 billion in Q3.

Of that, a record $7.1 billion came from tokenized equities. That's roughly 3.6% of the quarter's total volume.

Much of the third-quarter growth came from memecoins, according to Bitwise. On Nov. 26, the memecoin platform Pump accounted for $1.29 million of the $2.69 million in daily protocol revenue on Solana tracked by DefiLlama.

For SOL to recover and break even in November, it would need to rise about 34.6% by Nov. 30.

If November ends in the red, even a small decline in December would give Solana a record 10th losing month of the year.

December ended lower in five of the last six years shown on the chart. However, six data points aren't much to base a forecast on.

LayerZero's Zero mainnet launch and new institutional validators could strengthen ecosystem adoption and investor interest in the ZRO price.

LayerZero’s native token, ZRO, is approaching a crucial milestone as it trades near $1.10, up approximately 1.12% in the past 24 hours. The upcoming November 30 launch of its Zero mainnet has renewed investor attention, with new validators and trading platforms joining the ecosystem ahead of the rollout.

However, ZRO’s price continues to struggle within a prolonged descending channel, raising questions about whether this major launch can finally reverse its bearish trajectory. With the token hovering near its demand zone and the launch just days away, investors are watching whether the November 30 event can trigger a meaningful recovery or expose ZRO to further downside.

With the November 30 Zero mainnet launch approaching, LayerZero is adding more established names to its ecosystem. On November 25, the protocol announced that Kakao Pay, Samsung Card and ZAN would join Zero as genesis validators. Their involvement will help support the network’s initial operations, including consensus and proof verification. Kakao Pay is also exploring the possibility of using Zero’s infrastructure for a Korean won-backed stablecoin ecosystem, although no launch has been confirmed.

LayerZero is also expanding its cross-chain capabilities. On November 12, Flare announced its integration with the protocol as a Decentralized Verifier Network (DVN). This will allow Flare to help verify messages transferred between blockchains, initially supporting Flare and Ethereum. The integration is expected to go live in early December.

Another development worth watching is ZRO staking, which opened on November 23. Token holders can now stake their holdings to support Zero’s initial validator network. However, there is a catch: staked tokens will remain locked until March 31, 2027, with an additional withdrawal cooldown of up to seven days. Together, these developments show that LayerZero is building out its infrastructure and bringing more participants into the ecosystem ahead of launch.

On the upside, the descending channel’s upper boundary remains an important hurdle. Beyond this, the next major order-block region lies between $4.90 and $6.00.

LayerZero’s November 30 Zero mainnet launch could improve market sentiment, supported by new institutional validators and ecosystem integrations. However, ZRO’s weekly chart remains bearish, with declining OBV indicating weakening buying pressure. For now, the mainnet launch is a potential catalyst, but ZRO’s price needs stronger buying volume and a breakout to confirm a trend reversal.

#5168. XRP Bulls and Bears to Get 3x ETFs Soon

Two proposed U.S. exchange-traded funds would give investors a way to bet on XRP in either direction, with one targeting three times XRP's daily return and the other targeting three times its inverse.

If XRP gains 5% in a single day, the bullish ETF would target a 15% gain, excluding fees and expenses.

If XRP loses 5% in a single day, the bearish ETF would target a 15% gain.

However, investors betting on the wrong direction could lose approximately 15% of their investment in a single day.

The next update is scheduled for Nov. 30. Following a recent amendment submitted to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the registration statements for these ETFs are now scheduled to become effective on Monday.

The issuer has repeatedly delayed the effective date. It remains to be seen whether the funds will start trading anytime soon.

The filing covers a total of eight ETFs, including bullish and bearish funds for Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), Solana (SOL) and XRP.

Even if XRP's price remains unchanged over multiple trading days, both ETFs could record negative returns.

Since the ETFs rebalance daily, it's important to remember that when the price changes direction, the next day's percentage return is calculated based on the investment's value after the previous trading session.

Let's say XRP rises from $2 to $2.20 on Monday and then drops back to $2 on Tuesday. If you hold XRP over these two days, you'll break even.

However, if you invest $100 in the bullish ETF, your position would close Tuesday at approximately $94.55, assuming the fund achieves its daily target and excluding fees and expenses.

If XRP increases by 10% from $2 to $2.20 on Monday, the bullish ETF would target a 30% gain. Your initial $100 investment would now be worth $130.

For XRP to return to $2 on Tuesday, it would need to fall by approximately 9.09%.

The bullish ETF would therefore target a loss of roughly 27.27% on Tuesday. But that loss would be calculated against your $130 position, leaving you with approximately $94.55.

Of course, the bearish ETF wouldn't fare any better.

#5166. Bitcoin Miners Go 98 Minutes Without Finding a Single Block

Bitcoin miners experienced their longest dry spell since July on Nov. 26. According to Galaxy's Alex Thorn, it took Bitcoin miners 98 minutes and 19 seconds to find the next block.

That's the third time in 2026 that miners have gone this long without finding a block. The wait ended at 18:28 UTC on Thursday.

For anyone trying to get Bitcoin transactions confirmed shortly after the previous block, the gap meant waiting more than an hour and a half.

Even if you paid a very high transaction fee, you would still have to wait until a miner found the next block before your transaction could receive its first confirmation.

Thursday's gap was the 69th longest since 2011, according to Galaxy Research. It was just three minutes shy of the threshold for the top 50.

And this year's other long gap lasted nearly two hours. On July 6, miners took 112 minutes and 26 seconds to find the next block (number 956,953). That was the 19th longest gap on record, according to Galaxy.

Bitcoin automatically adjusts mining difficulty every 2,016 blocks to keep the average block interval at around 10 minutes.

However,  blocks sometimes are found seconds apart. Other times, it takes well over an hour for the next block to be found.

At any given mining difficulty, the chance that a single attempt to find a block will succeed is incredibly small.

If miners have spent 90 minutes trying to find the next block, the chance of succeeding on the next attempt is the same as it was on the first attempt.

So the expected time until the next block is found is still 10 minutes, even if it's already been 90 minutes since the last block was found. That's assuming the network's total computing power and mining difficulty remain unchanged.

Assuming an average block interval of 10 minutes, Thorn said you could expect a gap of at least 98 minutes and 19 seconds about once every 18,600 block intervals.

That means such a gap should occur roughly once every four months, based on an average of about 144 blocks per day.

Galaxy examined 877,290 block intervals going back to Jan. 1, 2011.

Researchers identified 1,948 intervals where at least an hour had passed between the timestamps of successive blocks.

However, Galaxy flagged 97 of those intervals because an adjacent block had a timestamp that was off by at least 10 minutes. This raised questions about the actual length of those gaps.

The longest recorded interval is particularly interesting.

On Nov. 30, 2011, block 155,290 seemingly marked the end of a 144-minute-and-50-second gap.

However, the miner who found the next block had set its timestamp back by 65 minutes.

After excluding apparent timestamp errors, the longest gap was 141 minutes and one second, recorded on Oct. 13, 2011.

SingleAssetVault activation is projected for December 9, subject to continued validator support.

XRPL stablecoin supply reached $836.90 million, with RLUSD representing 89.35%.

The proposed lending system supports uncollateralised loans, while borrower underwriting remains offchain.

The XRP Ledger lending system is getting closer to deployment, but don’t confuse a countdown with a working loan market. The SingleAssetVault amendment is projected to activate on December 9, provided validator support holds. The separate LendingProtocol amendment still needs approval.

Meanwhile, XRPL stablecoin supply has reached $836.90 million. RLUSD accounts for 89.35% of that total, according to November 27 figures. That’s a sizeable balance, but it isn’t money already committed to lending.

The SingleAssetVault amendment would establish infrastructure for pooling a single asset and issuing depositors shares representing their interest. The LendingProtocol amendment performs a different job: it enables brokers to arrange fixed-term loans and record repayments on the ledger.

XRPL amendments need more than 80% support from trusted validators for two consecutive weeks. If support falls short, the waiting period can restart. So December 9 remains a projection, not a guaranteed launch date.

The proposed system supports uncollateralised loans, making borrower assessment a serious issue for depositors. Underwriting and risk management happen offchain, according to the lending specification.

Brokers may also contribute optional first-loss capital in the same asset as the loan pool. That can absorb some missed-payment losses, but it isn’t a blanket guarantee.

The XRP Ledger Foundation has published an open-source reference application demonstrating the system on Devnet. It combines vaults and lending with credentials, permissioned domains and batch transactions.

Still, a working demonstration isn’t commercial adoption. XRPL DeFi total value locked stands at about $30.65 million, a separate measure from the $836.94 million stablecoin balance.

The XRP Ledger lending system now needs amendment activation, production markets and funded loans before stablecoin supply can translate into actual lending activity.

Available in Standard and Platinum editions, the BASIS Card offers up to 10% cashback, with applicants selecting their preferred tier subject to staking eligibility

The BASIS Card returns money differently. Announced today by BASIS DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE LTD, the payment card credits cashback in the asset used for each eligible purchase, with Platinum cardholders qualifying for 10% cashback during the introductory Launch Boost period.

For digital asset holders, the principle is straightforward. Spend Bitcoin and receive Bitcoin back. Pay with Ethereum and receive Ethereum back. There are no reward points to redeem or proprietary platform tokens to manage. Cashback is credited in an asset the cardholder already uses, giving everyday spending a direct connection to their digital asset holdings.

Opening first-round applications expands BASIS’s existing digital asset infrastructure into everyday payments. Applications are submitted at https://basis.pro/card and close on December 31, 2026, at 23:59 UTC.

The BASIS Card is available in Standard, finished in matte black composite, and Platinum, produced in metal. Applicants select their preferred edition when submitting their waitlist application, with qualification determined by their active staking position.

Each edition has a separate staking eligibility threshold, as detailed below. BASIS measures the value of the applicant’s active staking position against the requirement for their selected tier. The position is assessed at submission and re-checked at the close of the application period.

Participants can therefore review the benefits of each edition alongside its staking requirements before deciding which card to apply for. Final issuance remains subject to the issuing partner’s independent review.

Both editions feature an introductory Launch Boost period that begins on the date of card issuance. During this period, cardholders receive enhanced cashback rates, higher monthly reward caps, and additional subscription benefits.

*All monetary figures are expressed in USD. Physical card issuance fees include applicable shipping charges.

Launch Boost runs for three months following issuance, after which each card returns to its respective base benefits. Standard and Platinum also feature rate-lock periods of 12 and 24 months, respectively, subject to the applicable program terms.

Travel and additional card benefits include two annual airport lounge visits, a 3 GB eSIM, and one additional card, subject to tier eligibility and applicable terms. Standard cardholders benefit from a 2% FX fee, while Platinum cardholders pay no FX fee during Launch Boost. Both editions provide immediate access to a virtual card upon activation, with Platinum participants also receiving priority and dedicated support.

The defining feature of the BASIS Card is what happens after a purchase. Where conventional reward programs may require cardholders to accumulate points or convert rewards into their preferred currency, BASIS keeps the cashback denomination consistent with the asset spent.

Cashback on eligible settled purchases is credited directly to the cardholder’s Funding Wallet. A purchase made using BTC returns BTC, leaving the recipient free to decide how to use the reward.

Cardholders who wish to stake their cashback can do so separately under the platform’s ordinary conversion rules. Cashback does not automatically enter an existing staking position, and card rewards remain independent of staking yield.

Submitting a card application also leaves existing staking positions, lock-up periods, Dynamic Reward Rates, boosters, and stToken balances unchanged.

Applications are free and limited to one per account during Round 01. Participants must hold at least USD 1,000 in eligible BASIS wallet value at submission, maintain an account in good standing, and satisfy the staking requirements for their selected card edition.

Once BASIS approves a waitlist application, the applicant receives further instructions and a secure Know Your Customer (KYC) verification link. The issuing partner then conducts its own review, covering identity verification, residency, regional eligibility, sanctions screening, and supporting documentation.

Waitlist approval permits applicants to proceed to the next stage and does not constitute final card approval, activation, or issuance.

#5161. JPMorgan, HSBC and StoneX Trade Digital Gold in London as Tokenized Gold Holdings Jump 48%

London is testing tokenized gold as Tether Gold and PAX Gold holdings climb 48% to $4.6 billion despite falling gold prices.

JPMorgan, HSBC and StoneX completed the first live wholesale trades of fractional tokenized gold in London last week. The test is meant to keep the world’s largest gold market ahead of Asian rivals. The three firms also used the digital gold as collateral, without moving a single bar out of the vaults.

Bloomberg reported the trades on Tuesday. They ran on a system built by the World Gold Council (WGC), the industry body that led the project. David Tait, the WGC’s chief executive, called it “a historic step forward for the gold market.”

JPMORGAN $JPM, HSBC AND STONEX COMPLETE THE FIRST LIVE WHOLESALE TRADES OF FRACTIONAL DIGITAL GOLD IN LONDON, ALSO USING IT AS COLLATERAL pic.twitter.com/bwVAdrpkXh

— The Wolf Of All Streets (@scottmelker) November 24, 2026

The banks did not say how much gold changed hands. The system is still in testing, and there is no date yet for a wider launch. The timing is awkward for gold itself. The metal trades near $3,626 an ounce, 32% below its January record and 11% lower than a year ago.

What changes for London’s bullion market, and does it matter for crypto’s own gold tokens?

The WGC calls the new format “pooled gold interests.” Each one is a fractional, electronically transferable share in a pool of physical bars held in approved London vaults.

That fills a gap. Most London trades today are in unallocated gold, which is cheap to hold but leaves buyers as creditors if their bank fails. Allocated gold means owning specific bars, which is safer but costly and hard to split. The WGC proposed the pooled model with law firm Linklaters in September 2025 as a third route between the two.

The collateral piece matters most. Banks could pledge gold for loans and margin as easily as they post bonds, without trucks or vault transfers.

London has a lot riding on it. Its over-the-counter market handles more than $180 billion of gold trades a day, and its vaults held $1.4 trillion of gold in August. Hong Kong, working with the Shanghai Gold Exchange, began testing its own gold clearing system in July.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

The London pilot is a closed, bank-only system. Crypto has run its own version for years with Tether Gold (XAUT) and PAX Gold (PAXG), and those tokens have been growing fast.

We read the supply of both tokens straight from their Ethereum contracts, where each token equals one troy ounce. We compared that with CoinGecko’s figures from a year ago.

So crypto’s digital gold kept adding ounces even as the gold price fell. Still, the two tokens hold about 0.33% of the value of gold sitting in London’s vaults. The whole tokenized gold category traded about $329 million in the past 24 hours on CoinGecko, against London’s $180 billion a day.

Explore: RLUSD Surpasses Trump’s USD1 Stablecoin but XRP Still Sinks 26%

PAX Gold tracks the metal closely. On Binance, PAXG trades at $3,637, below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $3,945, and its 200-day EMA at $4,195.

Last week’s sell-off pushed it to $3,491 on Saturday, its lowest level in 300 days. Sellers led on Binance’s spot market, where the token itself changes hands. Orders that sold at the market price right away outweighed buyers by a net $13.4 million over the past seven days.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Reveals Upcoming Coinbase Listings

The WGC still has to settle governance rules and a launch date. If the big banks adopt digital gold for collateral, the gap between London’s vaults and crypto’s gold tokens could start to close.

U.S. government funding expires on December 11 unless Congress passes a new spending bill.

Trump has requested an additional $350 billion to rebuild Pentagon weapon stocks.

Pentagon cancellation costs could exceed $10 billion if planned weapons purchases are blocked.

The U.S. government is heading toward another shutdown, with federal funding set to expire on December 11. Congress has less than two weeks to pass a spending bill or stopgap measure to avoid a shutdown.

That is because Democrats and Republicans are struggling to agree on the funding bill over Iran war funding, defense spending, and the next budget.

The biggest fight over the U.S. budget is now about the Iran war and President Donald Trump’s request for another $350 billion for the Pentagon.

Republicans have proposed a $1.1 trillion defense bill, while the Trump administration is seeking an additional $350 billion to rebuild weapon stocks depleted by the war.

On the contrary, several Democrats want to restrict all the funding that could prolong the Iran war.

The group includes Senators Tim Kaine, Chris Van Hollen, Tammy Duckworth, Kirsten Gillibrand, Elizabeth Warren, Michael Bennet, Bernie Sanders, Elissa Slotkin, and Chris Murphy, along with Representatives Ro Khanna and Yassamin Ansari.

A similar disagreement over healthcare subsidies caused a 43-day government shutdown last year, the longest in US history. Federal workers missed paychecks, government services stopped, and key economic reports were delayed.

The shutdown risk now carries a direct financial cost for the military as well. The Pentagon has warned that if Congress does not approve the planned weapons purchases, taxpayers could have to pay more than $10 billion in fees to cancel deals with RTX and Lockheed Martin.

As of November 28, none of the 12 regular FY2027 spending bills had become law. The House had passed three, while the Senate had passed none.

If lawmakers fail to approve new funding, the government would enter a funding gap on December 12.

The U.S. has already faced several government shutdowns. The 2025 shutdown lasted 43 days, the longest in U.S. history. During that period, Bitcoin reached $126,200 before falling nearly 20%.

The shutdown also reduced money flowing into financial markets and delayed crypto ETF decisions. Important reports on inflation, jobs, and the economy were also held up, making it harder for investors to predict interest rate changes.

The U.S. faced another three-day funding gap in early 2026, followed by a 75-day shutdown affecting the Department of Homeland Security.

A new shutdown starting December 12 could create further uncertainty for financial markets.

However, the political situation could change on January 3, when Democrats are expected to take control of both the House and Senate. They could then push their own funding bills to reopen the government.

However, President Donald Trump would still have the power to veto those bills, meaning the funding fight may continue.

#5156. Binance Announces Dividends for Nvidia and Other Stocks

Binance will pay dividends to holders of stock tokens representing five companies: Nvidia, PayPal, Qualcomm, Western Digital, and Wendy’s.

The exchange will use the dividends paid by these companies to buy more stock tokens, allowing users to increase their holdings of the same stocks through the bStocks program.

The most important date for Nvidia token holders is Dec. 2. That's when Binance will take a snapshot of NVDAB balances at 01:00 UTC.

The snapshot for Wendy’s is scheduled for Dec. 1, followed by Nvidia on Dec. 2 and Qualcomm on Dec. 3.

Snapshots for PayPal and Western Digital are both scheduled for Dec. 4.

All snapshots will take place at 01:00 UTC.

In its Nov. 27 announcement, Binance provided the dates that will determine eligibility for dividends.

Binance plans to use Nvidia's cash dividends to purchase additional Nvidia shares, including fractional shares, after deducting applicable withholding taxes, fees, and other charges.

The proceeds will then be distributed among users who hold NVDAB on Binance and qualify for the dividend payment.

The same process will apply to the other four stocks.

If you hold eligible tokens in other products on the platform, such as savings or margin accounts, Binance will still credit the dividends to your spot account.

If you hold bStocks on-chain, the dividend payments will be made by adjusting the token's multiplier.

The tokens themselves are issued by Binance affiliate BTECH Holdings Limited, which owns the underlying securities.

So, if you hold NVDAB, you have an interest in the Nvidia shares held by BTECH.

If you need to transfer tokens to Binance before the snapshot, you must do so at least two hours in advance.

Deposits and withdrawals of Nvidia tokens will be suspended at 23:00 UTC on Dec. 1.

Binance will also suspend one-to-one conversions between Nvidia shares and NVDAB tokens during this period.

The same two-hour suspension rule will apply to the other four stock tokens.

However, spot trading against USDT will continue, including trading in the NVDAB/USDT pair.

Binance said it would resume deposits, withdrawals, and stock-to-token conversions after the dividend allocations are completed.

The exchange will not issue a separate announcement when these services resume.

BlackRock's IBIT accounted… pic.twitter.com/PUKLdaUgKS

— CryptoSavingExpert ® (@CryptoSavingExp) November 25, 2026

Bitcoin keeps sliding anyway. It trades near $58,900 on Wednesday, down 53% from its October 2025 record of $126,272. On Saturday, it touched $55,081, its lowest price in more than two years.

So if the funds are selling less, where could Bitcoin’s bear market end? We checked where Bitcoin bottomed in every past cycle, using Fibonacci retracement levels, ratios traders use to measure how much of a rally gets erased.

SoSoValue’s ETF flow figures, as reported this week, show the pressure easing:

Even after the selling, the funds still hold about $52 billion of net inflows since launch. That is roughly 83% of their October 2025 peak, so most ETF buyers have not left.

For Bitcoin news readers, slower outflows don’t mean buyers are back, though. They mean less forced selling from one big source. For the price to turn, the flows need to flip to inflows.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

Fibonacci retracements measure how much of a rally a market gives back. Traders watch a handful of ratios, mainly 0.618 and 0.786, as places where a drop may stop.

We measured each Bitcoin cycle on Bitstamp’s daily price history since 2011. Each runs from one bear-market bottom to the next record high. We then checked how much of that move was erased by the next bottom.

That is the less-reported Bitcoin news: each bear market stopped a little earlier than the last, by three to four points each time. If that trend holds, the next bottom would land near the 0.786 Fibonacci level, a 78.6% retracement.

This cycle runs from the 2022 low of $15,479 to the $126,272 record. On that range, 0.786 sits at about $39,200. So far, Bitcoin has given back 64.3%. Saturday’s low already cut through the 0.618 level at $57,800.

A log scale treats a doubling the same at any price. On that scale, past bottoms came at shallower ratios, rising from 33% to 48%. The 0.5 level on that scale for this cycle is about $44,200. Both methods point to a $39,000 to $44,000 zone.

#5153. Bank of Japan Warns Stablecoins and Tokenization Threaten Financial Stability

Japan's central bank has warned that automated trading in tokenized markets could exacerbate a sell-off.

It also raised concerns about whether stablecoin holders can always redeem their tokens at face value.

A Bank of Japan executive director outlined these risks during his keynote speech at an International Monetary Fund seminar in Tokyo.

In the event of a price drop, according to Kazushige Kamiyama, a smart contract could automatically increase the amount of collateral required. It could also trigger a sale of the collateral backing a position if the borrower doesn't have enough collateral.

These sales could drive prices even lower, potentially spreading financial stress across institutions and markets.

In the case of stablecoins, the question is whether a token with a face value of one dollar can always be redeemed for one dollar.

To ensure this, issuers' reserves need to be properly regulated, and the links to central bank money need to be reliable, Kamiyama said.

A bank might have enough cash to pay for a trade in tokenized assets but still be unable to complete the payment.

This could happen when a trade is settled overnight, and the payment system the bank uses to transfer cash is unavailable.

The bank might have to keep additional cash on a trading platform. Meanwhile, cash held on another network might not be accessible when the payment is due.

"Even with faster settlement, it does not necessarily lead to efficient liquidity management," Kamiyama said.

Cross-border securities trades, however, could benefit from tokenization.

A smart contract could link the payment and delivery of a security so that both transactions are executed simultaneously.

This could reduce the risk of a buyer paying for an asset without receiving it.

The Bank of Japan is setting up a testing environment with financial institutions that hold accounts at the central bank.

One scenario involves exploring how cash settlement could work for trades involving tokenized Japanese government bonds.

The central bank is considering two options for making the cash payment.

One would involve issuing tokenized central bank money. The other would link a token trading platform to Japan's existing payment infrastructure.

These tests will evaluate whether the proposed solutions can address the challenges financial institutions face when settling trades.

Bitwise Chief Investment Officer Matt Hougan is betting that tokenized stock trading will make Solana one of the largest networks in crypto. In a Real Vision interview published Tuesday, he said Solana could be worth $300 billion within five years if it handles 10% of global stock trading.

He called that “a completely reasonable valuation.” Solana’s market value today is about $40 billion, so his target is roughly 7.5 times higher.

Solana’s own fees show how far the network still has to go. It collected $229 million in transaction fees over the past 12 months, about 1/33 of the revenue in Hougan’s scenario.

SOL trades near $67.81, down 77% from its January 2025 record and 2.7% lower on the day.

Hougan spoke to Real Vision at Solana’s Breakpoint conference in London. CoinMarketCap’s report of the interview lays out his math:

A tokenized stock is a blockchain token that tracks a share such as Nvidia or Tesla. It can trade around the clock and settle in seconds.

Hougan was less upbeat on Ethereum, which still holds more tokenized assets overall. He said some ETH holders are “probably going to step out of the asset,” adding: “We’ll see which ends up being more valuable.”

For Hougan’s forecast, the size of today’s market matters. It is growing, but it starts small. The rwa.xyz stocks dashboard counted $3.57 billion of tokenized shares in investors’ hands on Wednesday, held across 5 million wallets.

That last number puts Hougan’s goal in perspective. Ten percent of global stock trading comes to about $2.5 trillion a month. Even counting every token transfer as a trade, tokenized shares on all chains are at about 4% of that.

The key test for Hougan’s case is fees, because his math rests on them. We added up the base and priority fees users paid on the network, using DefiLlama’s Solana fee data.

January 2025 alone, the month of the TRUMP memecoin launch, brought in $241 million, and that memecoin frenzy has faded. Trading in tokenized shares would need to replace it many times over for Hougan’s math to work.

Monero (XMR) is not welcome on top exchanges as the series of delistings takes an uglier turn for holders following Kucoin's XMR removal. But Kucoin wasn't first and might not be the last: XMR was removed from MEXC, Kraken, Binance and others already.

The main issue for an asset that's being removed from exchanges will always be the liquidity. In the last 24 hours, Monero's spot flow lost $1.3 million. Despite the increasing volume, the asset is recording outflows and exchange withdrawals. The volume spike is most like being a reflection of a substantial selling activity.

In a single day, XMR was losing almost 20% of its value. If it wasn't for the delisting, price could've broken multiple technical resistances already and confirmed a recovery. As of November 27, the price is slowly recovering, following the general relief on the cryptocurrency market.

On November 26, Kucoin announced the removal of XMR/USDT, XMR/USDC, XMR/ETH and XMR/BTC trading pairs, effective November 30. The exchange has already limited any deposits, with withdrawals available for all users.

Monero is an inherently private cryptocurrency, that limits the ability of explorers to determine transaction destination and senders. That is the main reason centralized exchanges are removing XMR.

For holders, the problem is not that Monero stops working after a delisting. The network is still active, and XMR can be transferred between wallets or traded on exchanges that continue to support it. The problem is that there are fewer places to buy and sell it. If more large exchanges follow Kucoin, liquidity could become lower, making new selling activity more painful for the price.

#5146. Zcash Whale Wakes Up After 9 Years, Moves $11.39 Million To Kraken

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

The coins date back to 2017, when Ethereum was still a relatively young network, decentralized finance barely existed and Zcash was attempting to establish itself as a more private alternative to Bitcoin.

Almost a decade later, the wallet is active again. And its owner’s reported acquisition price makes the transaction particularly interesting.

According to Lookonchain, the whale originally acquired 23,412 ZEC at an average price of approximately $215, representing an investment of just over $5 million.

The latest transactions account for roughly two-thirds of that original position, with at least 7,750 ZEC transferred to a Kraken deposit address.

At the reported transfer valuation of approximately $723 per ZEC, those 15,750 coins are worth around $8 million more than their estimated acquisition cost. That would represent a return of approximately 236% if the investor sold them at that price.

What makes this wallet fascinating, however, is what happened between those two valuations.

Zcash spent much of 2024 and early 2025 trading around $16 to $20 before staging a remarkable comeback. At $20 per coin, the whale’s original investment would have been worth less than $470,000, a paper loss of more than 90%, assuming the position remained intact.

Holding an asset through a temporary market correction is one thing. Holding it through years of declining relevance, while newer cryptocurrencies attract developers, investors and attention, is something else entirely.

Whatever the owner’s reasons for keeping the coins untouched, the decision has aged considerably better than it appeared to during Zcash’s quieter years.

It also explains why the available information tells only part of the story.

Lookonchain can identify an apparent exchange deposit and estimate its value. Establishing who controls the wallet, whether ownership changed privately during those nine years or what the investor intends to do next is considerably harder.

Even the reported acquisition price is an estimate rather than a verified record of the owner’s personal trading history.

That is an important limitation of on-chain analysis, particularly when dealing with a network explicitly designed to give users greater control over their financial visibility.

The renewed enthusiasm surrounding Zcash has attracted a different kind of investor from the one buying ZEC in 2017.

NewsBTC previously reported that Winklevoss Capital backed the launch of a dedicated Zcash treasury strategy, illustrating how exposure to the cryptocurrency has begun extending beyond traditional crypto wallets.

But the revival of an old cryptocurrency also comes with an interesting complication: investors who have spent years underwater finally have an opportunity to recover their capital or take profits.

That does not necessarily make the Kraken deposit bearish. A transfer to an exchange is not proof of a completed sale, and one wallet cannot establish a broader trend among Zcash holders.

Still, the transaction is worth watching. If more early investors start moving dormant coins onto exchanges, Zcash’s new buyers may find themselves absorbing supply from an entirely different generation of holders.

Nine years ago, someone reportedly committed more than $5 million to the idea of private digital money. Today, the blockchain offers a glimpse of what that investment has become.

Whether the owner has finished holding Zcash is a question the blockchain alone cannot yet answer.

Falling gold and Bitcoin prices erase an estimated $5.7 billion from Tether’s holdings, putting its USDT reserve cushion under pressure.

Gold just slid toward $3,500 an ounce and silver fell below $40, extending a sell-off that has put Tether gold back in focus. Why? Tether keeps billions of dollars of gold bars in the reserves behind USDT, so the crash hits its balance sheet directly.

Based on Tether’s latest reserves report and the blockchain, the company holds about 168 tons of gold: 142.8 tons it owns in its USDT reserves, plus 25.7 tons backing its Tether Gold (XAUT) token.

#5144. Ripple's David Schwartz Shuts Down XRP Escrow Burn Idea: Even 80% Can’t Force It

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz said on Friday that XRP Ledger validators cannot force the rest of the network to burn Ripple's escrowed XRP, even with more than 80% support. According to Schwartz, the XRP Ledger has "no coercive mechanism at all."

Schwartz, one of the creators of the XRP Ledger, made the comments in two replies on X on Thursday and Friday. The thread started on Wednesday with a post from an XRP community member. According to the post, "validators have no say over Ripple's escrow," and Ripple runs one validator on the default Unique Node List (dUNL), not three.

Another X user then asked: "Couldn't validators pass an amendment that would burn Ripple's escrow? Changes to the code of the XRPL could do anything..." Schwartz answered on Thursday that such validators would "just disagree with everyone else who didn't want that change and be counted as disagreeing validators, effectively isolating themselves from the network."

If the majority of nodes want something, nothing can stop them from having it. They just can't force those who don't agree to go along with them. But the same is true for a minority of nodes too. There's no coercive mechanism at all.

On Friday, the same user asked whether the answer would change if "the vast majority (80+%)" wanted the burn. "If the majority of nodes want something, nothing can stop them from having it. They just can't force those who don't agree to go along with them. But the same is true for a minority of nodes too. There's no coercive mechanism at all," Schwartz wrote.

On Nov. 16, a group of XRP holders called Make XRP Great Again demanded in an open letter to Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse that the company burn 31.1 billion escrowed XRP by March 31, 2027. XRP Insights recorded the same amount in 99 escrow objects that day. Ripple reported 31.7 billion XRP in escrow as of Sept. 30.

According to XRPScan, an amendment on the XRP Ledger needs 29 of 35 validator votes, or more than 80%, and has to keep that support for two weeks before it activates.

In late 2020, Schwartz wrote on X that "if the majority wants a rules change, there is nothing the minority can do to stop them." On Feb. 19, 2024, he wrote that Ripple "could unilaterally create the same effect as burning an escrow by provably blackholing the account the escrow completes into."

In February 2026, Schwartz argued with Cyber Capital founder Justin Bons on X. Bons called the XRP Ledger centralized and said that its Unique Node List gives Ripple control over consensus. Schwartz described the claims as "objectively nonsensical."

Ripple's next monthly escrow release of 1 billion XRP is scheduled for Dec. 1. In its Nov. 16 letter, Make XRP Great Again also asked Garlinghouse for a public response and a verifiable plan for the burn.

Stablecoin giant Tether [USDT] has been making some moves lately. Here’s the rundown.

Tether has backed Argentine fintech app Lemon, with the former not putting a number on it when it announced the deal. Lemon did, however, saying that the package is worth $14.5 million.

According to Lemon CEO Marcelo Cavazzoli, only $5 million of that is an actual investment in the company’s shares. The other $9.5 million is an incentive plan linked to products the two will build together.

There’s a lot that’s unclear right now though. Neither side has shared Lemon’s valuation or how big a stake Tether is getting. There’s also no word on how or when the $9.5 million gets paid out. Tether is after more users for USDT and Tether Gold [XAUT] across Latin America. Lemon gives it a decent shot at that. The app is said to have 4.5 million verified users, and its main balance runs on USDT.

Worth noting, however, that Lemon’s not the only home for Tether this month.

On the 9th, D3 launched a USD vault for Tether’s stablecoin. Users can deposit USDT, keep an eye on their position, and withdraw without leaving the platform.

Sentora built the system using its Earn OS and Upshift tools, which decide where deposited funds go. Money moves with the market, within a set of risk rules. It is said that the setup has already handled more than $2 billion.

Domain buyers usually come in, make a deal, and leave. Earning on stablecoins gives them a reason to keep their money on the platform.

Just don’t mistake automated for guaranteed. Returns depend on the lending markets the vault uses. So, users are still trusting a whole stack of infrastructure with their dollars.

PEPE whales have accumulated more than six trillion tokens worth approximately $21.16 million, according to new data from blockchain monitoring platform Lookonchain. Most of that position belongs to a single unidentified wallet that has been accumulating the memecoin since November 17.

The size of the position is unusual even by memecoin standards. One address now holds more than 1% of PEPE’s entire supply, and its owner has continued adding tokens despite weakness in the market.

The wallet, identified by its opening characters 0x5011, accumulated 5.15 trillion PEPE over eight days. Lookonchain valued the holdings at $18.28 million, representing approximately 1.22% of the cryptocurrency’s total supply.

The more interesting detail is how quickly the position has grown.

Lookonchain’s transaction monitoring history shows that by November 19, the wallet had withdrawn around 1.9 trillion PEPE from Binance. That figure climbed to 2.878 trillion by November 23 and exceeded 3.3 trillion the following day.

On Wednesday, Lookonchain reported that the address had accumulated 4.16 trillion tokens. By Thursday, its reported holdings had reached 5.15 trillion.

Another wallet, beginning with 0x6246, accumulated 868.16 billion PEPE valued at approximately $2.88 million, bringing the combined reported value to more than $21 million.

Large withdrawals are nothing new for the memecoin. NewsBTC previously covered a separate PEPE whale moving $14.7 million out of Binance. What makes the latest activity particularly interesting is the repeated accumulation within such a short period.

Before treating these transactions as a bullish signal, it’s worth looking at what other large holders have been doing.

Data from blockchain analytics platform Deep Blue Alpha showed that withdrawals accounted for approximately 36% of tracked PEPE whale transfers between wallets and exchanges over the preceding seven days, according to its November 26 update.

In other words, exchange deposits outweighed withdrawals within that particular group of wallets.

That doesn’t invalidate Lookonchain’s findings. It does, however, complicate the idea that large investors are collectively preparing for a PEPE recovery.

One group of holders may be increasing its exposure while others are looking to reduce theirs. The distinction matters, especially in a market where a handful of transactions can attract more attention than the activity of dozens of other wallets.

Exchange deposits aren’t necessarily sales, just as withdrawals don’t establish that a fresh purchase has taken place. Centralized exchange trading records remain largely invisible to outside observers.

For an investor holding 5.15 trillion PEPE, even a movement of $0.000001 in the token’s price would change the value of the position by $5.15 million.

That illustrates both the attraction and the risk of holding such a large quantity of a speculative asset.

Building an $18 million position is one thing. Exiting it at the quoted market price is another. The amount an investor can actually realize depends on available liquidity, execution and the market’s ability to absorb the tokens.

Concentrated holdings can therefore work in both directions. If tokens remain outside exchanges, they may reduce the supply immediately available for trading. If the same tokens return to exchanges, traders may suddenly find themselves watching for potential selling pressure.

The next development worth following is whether these wallets continue accumulating or begin transferring tokens back to trading platforms.

For now, two addresses hold an unusually large amount of PEPE. Whether the rest of the market shares their apparent appetite for the memecoin is a different question.

Data from BitInfoCharts shows that Monero fell from $525.36 to $446.54 during Thursday’s trading session. For longtime XMR investors, the sell-off is an uncomfortable reminder of what happened when Binance announced its Monero delisting in February 2024.

This time, however, the list of major exchanges available to Monero traders is considerably shorter.

In a November 26 announcement, KuCoin confirmed that it will remove all four Monero spot trading pairs against USDT, USDC, ETH and BTC on November 30 at 08:00 UTC.

The exchange has already suspended XMR deposits and does not intend to reopen them. Withdrawals are scheduled to remain available until December 31 at 08:00 UTC, although KuCoin reserves the right to close them earlier if problems affecting the network arise.

Monero’s removal extends beyond spot trading. KuCoin will discontinue XMR flexible savings on November 27, followed by its conversion and automated trading services on November 30.

There is another detail in the announcement that deserves particular attention. KuCoin will stop accepting XMR as collateral for its VIP loan products. Customers who have borrowed against their Monero holdings may need to provide alternative collateral to avoid liquidation.

For holders planning to leave their coins on the exchange until the withdrawal deadline, KuCoin also warned that remaining balances could be converted into stablecoins, although “such conversion is not guaranteed.”

The exchange cited its platform policies but did not identify a specific regulatory requirement behind the decision.

KuCoin is not the first exchange to abandon Monero this month, but its departure could prove particularly significant given the amount of XMR trading it handles.

A November 26 snapshot from CoinGecko identified KuCoin as Monero’s most active exchange, with its XMR/USDT pair recording approximately $62.6 million in trading volume over a 24-hour period.

Earlier this month, MEXC discontinued spot trading for Monero on November 17. Binance removed the cryptocurrency in February 2024, while Kraken halted XMR trading for European Economic Area customers in October of the same year, explicitly citing regulatory changes.

Trading volume does not simply disappear when an exchange delists an asset. Some of it will move elsewhere, and investors who intend to keep their holdings can withdraw them to private wallets.

The bigger question is how efficiently the remaining exchanges can absorb that activity. If fewer venues are competing for the same orders, particularly during periods of market stress, large trades could become more expensive to execute and price swings more pronounced.

For Monero, that is increasingly a market structure problem rather than a question of whether its underlying technology works.

There is a case against assuming that Thursday’s sell-off marks the beginning of a prolonged decline.

Monero has survived previous exchange removals and even managed to establish new price highs in 2026 despite mounting restrictions. As NewsBTC previously reported, XMR traded above $700 earlier this year, long after Binance stopped supporting its spot markets.

But a functioning network does not guarantee a liquid market. Investors still need practical ways to enter and exit their positions without incurring excessive trading costs.

November 30 will therefore be an important test for Monero. Rather than focusing solely on whether XMR recovers the $500 level, traders should watch where KuCoin’s trading volume migrates and whether the remaining exchanges can absorb larger orders without substantial slippage.

That will offer a better indication of whether Thursday’s decline was a temporary reaction to another delisting or a warning of a deeper liquidity problem.

#5137. Bitcoin wallet privacy at risk? Researcher claims $0.35 attack could expose users’ IP addresses

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

This vulnerability was identified by Bitcoin Core contributor Abubakar Sadiq Ismail in a post on the Delving Bitcoin developer forum. As it stands, although Bitcoin transactions are publicly recorded, wallet addresses are pseudonymous, meaning users can view transaction details without knowing who controls them.

Similarly, Bitcoin’s P2P network makes it difficult to link a wallet to a specific computer.

Well, according to researcher Sadeeq, the answer may be yes because of a weakness in how Bitcoin Core handles transaction rebroadcasting.

To understand the vulnerability, it is important to know how Bitcoin Core works. So, many users operate their own nodes, which maintain blockchain copies, validate transactions, and communicate with other nodes. These nodes can also run wallets that track Bitcoin addresses.

Each node has an IP address that can reveal its internet provider and approximate location. However, a wallet address does not normally expose the IP address of the computer tracking it. Hence, the vulnerability arises because Bitcoin Core may rebroadcast transactions that remain unconfirmed for approximately 12 to 36 hours.

According to the researcher, an attacker can exploit this by sending a small, low-fee payment to a targeted address. For this, the payment must meet Bitcoin’s minimum dust threshold while carrying a low enough fee to remain unconfirmed. Going forward, the attacker could then wait for the wallet to rebroadcast the planted transaction while monitoring different Bitcoin nodes.

When one node announces the transaction again, the attacker can identify it as the node whose wallet tracks the targeted address. This, in turn, would theoretically link the Bitcoin address to the node’s IP address, exposing information about its internet connection.

On the question of simulation involving five target wallets across six trials, Sadeeq successfully identified the correct wallet-tracking node in all 30 attempts. However, this does not necessarily reveal who owns the Bitcoin.

Hence, as a potential workaround, users can disable automatic wallet broadcasting through the -walletbroadcast=0 setting. However, this might lead to another problem, and that is that it stops automatic broadcasting of their own transactions. Therefore, proposed Bitcoin Core changes aim to address the issue, but they remain unreleased.

Here, it’s worth noting that these revelations coincided with the percentage of Bitcoin wallets currently at a loss entering a capitulation zone — historically associated with major market reversals. This could also mean that while retail investors panic, larger investors may be preparing to accumulate.

BNB Chain has outlined the architecture for a new Ethereum-compatible Layer 1 (L1) network, confirming that the proposed framework will not introduce a separate native token.

In an H2 2026 Tech Roadmap published in July 2026, BNB Chain stated that a next-generation L1 architecture was in development on a design path toward the 1 million TPS end-of-life goal and toward supporting different use cases than the existing ones. The plan was to ship it on testnet by the end of 2026, with mainnet release following in early 2027.

Fast forward to the close of November 2026, BNB Chain has introduced the Litepaper for the New L1, which describes the architecture being developed for high-frequency trading, payments, private finance and autonomous AI agents.

The design combines early transaction feedback, reserved capacity, native account controls and shielded settlement.

The new L1 is being developed alongside BNB Smart Chain, which remains the ecosystem’s broad-based network and streams small groups of transactions called SubBlocks before sealing a full block, with its public testnet being worked towards.

On the new L1, lanes reserve a share of block capacity for eligible activity, such as payments, while unused capacity returns to general traffic. This reduces competition from unrelated activity without guaranteeing that every transaction lands immediately.

The new L1 retains an Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM)-compatible execution environment. Parallel EVM execution is planned, and protected ordering through a trusted execution environment (TEE) gateway has also been proposed.

BNB Chain invites the crypto community to participate in discussions on its Layer 1,  submitting their questions, use cases, and feedback to the BNB Forum.

Bitcoin news today: BTC bounces 8% with gold and silver after Thanksgiving. Since 2013, only New Year shows a reliable gain.

The rebound barely dents a brutal month. Bitcoin is still down 20% in November, from $77,580 on November 1. So is this a Thanksgiving pump, and does Bitcoin have a holiday-season pattern? We checked every Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year since 2013.

The answer is mostly no. Bitcoin rose over Thanksgiving weekend in only 6 of 13 years, and over Christmas in 5 of 13.

Is there no correlation at all? New Year is the exception: Bitcoin gained between December 30 and January 2 in 12 of the last 13 years.

All three assets rebounded after a rough Wednesday, when hot inflation data sealed a December Fed rate hike. Bitcoin rose 8% from its $57,300 low to $61,780, its highest level since Monday.

The metals moved faster. US gold futures climbed 4.6% from Wednesday’s close to $3,699 an ounce. Silver did even better, jumping 11.4% to $44.60. Analysts tied the rebound to a weaker US dollar.

The timing matters. US markets were closed on Thursday and trade only half a day on Friday, so thin volume made every move look bigger.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

To put Bitcoin news today in context, we measured bitcoin’s price change in three holiday windows every year from 2013 to 2025, using Bitstamp’s daily closing prices.

Thanksgiving weekend, from Wednesday’s close to Sunday’s, has been a coin flip. Bitcoin rose in 6 of 13 years, and the median move was -0.1%. The swings were large in both directions, from a 13.2% drop in 2018 to 12.9% gains in 2015 and 2017.

Christmas was no better. Between December 23 and 26, bitcoin rose in only 5 of 13 years, again with a median move of -0.1%.

New Year stands out. From December 30 to January 2, bitcoin gained in 12 of the last 13 years, with a median rise of 1.8%. The only drop came in 2019. The gain is small, but it keeps repeating, perhaps because some funds and traders put fresh cash to work at the start of the year.

EXPLORE: BTC News Today: US Bitcoin Strategic Reserve Bill Moves Closer as BTC Reclaims $60K

From the day before Thanksgiving to January 2, Bitcoin rose in 7 of 13 years, and the size of the move tracked its four-year cycle. In bull years the season was spectacular: bitcoin gained 79% in 2017 and 72% in 2020. In the years after a cycle top, it disappointed, with 14% drops in both 2014 and 2018 and a flat season in 2022.

The gains also tended to fade once the holidays ended. Bitcoin fell in January in 8 of 13 years, with a median drop of 5.4%.

This year looks more like the post-top years. Bitcoin peaked in October 2025 and is down more than half since. So for Bitcoin news today, the lesson is that a holiday bounce has not yet changed the trend.

BTC trades at $61,780, below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $71,180, and its 200-day EMA at $74,450.

The takeaway from Bitcoin news today: history says the Thanksgiving bounce is a coin flip, and the season as a whole follows the cycle. If the pattern holds, the one date worth watching is the turn of the year.

Michael Saylor’s net worth has fallen by approximately $6 billion since the cryptocurrency market peaked in October 2025. The Strategy co-founder, whose fortune was estimated at $9.3 billion at the time, is now worth around $3.3 billion, according to Forbes.

The decline has wiped out nearly two-thirds of Saylor’s estimated wealth. Yet the billionaire’s company continues to accumulate Bitcoin despite mounting paper losses, showing little willingness to reconsider its investment strategy.

For Saylor, the downturn presents a problem that extends well beyond the price of Bitcoin. Much of his fortune depends on a company that must convince investors to keep financing its accumulation strategy.

Saylor was already among the cryptocurrency industry’s biggest financial casualties in February, when Forbes estimated that his wealth had fallen by $4.7 billion from its October 2025 level.

His fortune briefly stabilized in the following months, reaching an estimated $4.7 billion in June, before suffering another setback.

The latest estimate puts Saylor’s wealth approximately 64.5% below its October 2025 level.

Bitcoin’s return to the $60,000 level has added pressure, but the cryptocurrency alone does not explain the scale of the decline. Saylor’s exposure through Strategy makes his financial position considerably more complicated than that of an ordinary Bitcoin investor.

The $6 billion represents a reduction in estimated wealth, not a confirmed cash loss or the proceeds of any disclosed asset sales.

In October 2020, Saylor disclosed that he personally owned 17,732 BTC, acquired for approximately $175 million.

At the Bitcoin price of $60,325 reported by Strategy on November 26, those holdings would be worth approximately $1.07 billion, assuming he still owns the entire disclosed amount.

That would leave his original personal investment with an unrealized gain of roughly $895 million.

His current personal Bitcoin balance has not been independently confirmed, but the calculation illustrates an important distinction. Saylor can lose billions in estimated wealth while remaining substantially profitable on his original Bitcoin purchases.

The situation at Strategy is quite different.

While Saylor began buying Bitcoin at considerably lower prices, his company has spent much of the past several years increasing its exposure at higher valuations.

According to its November 23 SEC filing, Strategy acquired another 457 BTC for $29.6 million, bringing its total holdings to 851,305 BTC.

The company has spent approximately $64.23 billion accumulating Bitcoin at an average purchase price of $75,446.

Its official Bitcoin dashboard valued those reserves at approximately $51.35 billion on November 26.

That leaves a gap of nearly $12.9 billion between the company’s cumulative acquisition cost and the market value of its Bitcoin holdings.

These figures do not represent realized trading losses, nor do they capture the full financial performance of the company.

Nevertheless, the numbers reveal how dramatically the economics of accumulating Bitcoin have changed during the downturn.

For years, investors were willing to pay a premium for Strategy shares. The attraction was not simply the Bitcoin it owned, but the prospect that management could raise additional capital and increase shareholders’ exposure to the cryptocurrency.

That premium is no longer something the company can take for granted.

Strategy’s dashboard showed an mNAV ratio of 0.94 at the November 25 stock market close, using its own net Bitcoin value per share methodology.

The company’s latest investor briefing acknowledges the implications:

A widening discount can cause MSTR to underperform BTC even when bitcoin rises.

This is where Saylor’s investment model faces a more difficult test.

When investors are willing to pay a premium for Strategy shares, raising capital to acquire more Bitcoin can improve the economics of the business. When that premium disappears, issuing additional shares becomes a more complicated proposition.

Strategy’s own sensitivity analysis shows that a Bitcoin price of $40,000 would reduce its estimated net reserve value per share to $45.37, compared with $163.17 at a Bitcoin price of $100,000. The figures illustrate how sensitive the company’s underlying reserve valuation is to Bitcoin price movements.

Strategy’s third-quarter financial results offer a clearer picture of why its cash reserves and financing obligations now matter almost as much as the price of Bitcoin.

Buying more Bitcoin is only one part of the equation. The cost of financing those purchases matters just as much.

There is a credible case for recovery. Strategy still owns more than 850,000 Bitcoin, giving it considerable exposure to any sustained cryptocurrency market rebound.

The company also reported approximately $4.82 billion in combined cash and dollar reserves in its latest investor briefing, providing a buffer against its financing obligations.

But a recovery in Bitcoin would not necessarily produce an equivalent recovery in Saylor’s wealth. Strategy’s share price also depends on its debt, preferred-stock obligations, access to capital and the valuation investors are willing to assign to its business model.

The next test for Saylor is not whether he can buy another thousand Bitcoin. It is whether he can continue financing those purchases on terms that benefit existing shareholders.

His personal fortune has already demonstrated how expensive that distinction can become.

#5133. Ripple’s XRP Ledger Lending Protocol Eyes Final Activation

The XRP Ledger lending protocol proposed by leading blockchain firm Ripple is making the headlines as it appears to be rapidly moving closer to its final debut.

The latest reports on its progress show that the protocol is just one validator vote away from concluding its mandatory approval process on the network.

Barely a few weeks after Ripple proposed a lending protocol on the XRP Ledger, the lending protocol amendment has already secured 28 of the 35 validator votes required to begin the approval process.

This marks major progress for the development, as the XRPL amendment system requires that a proposal earn more than 80% support from trusted validators for two consecutive weeks before it becomes permanently enabled.

While the approval period is mandated to restart if support falls below that level during the countdown, it appears that the Ripple lending protocol is already set to wrap up this process, as it is just one more vote away from reaching the 29-vote milestone.

This means that the lending vaults may be on track for their activation on December 9 if the lending protocol amendment retains the ongoing support.

With the proposed protocol drawing closer to its final launch, the XRP community has continued to express excitement as the proposal aims to introduce fixed-term, fixed-rate lending directly on the XRP Ledger.

As such, users will be able to deposit assets including the Ripple stablecoin and earn interest from borrowers, providing additional ways to earn money.

It is important to note that the proposal aims to provide exclusive opportunities for both lenders and borrowers while further expanding Ripple’s $837 million stablecoin market.

The development tracker currently places the first partner payments in $CON in February 2027.

From the November 26 reference price of approximately $0.06582, a return to the November 24 high of $0.08434 would represent potential appreciation of around 28.1%. ConConAI’s broader proposition is built around bringing back the personal purchase advisor, powered by artificial intelligence. Instead of navigating endless search results and comparing countless products, users describe what they need. A specialist AI advisor asks relevant questions, interprets the requirements, and returns one recommendation with the reason behind it.

The consumer remains in control. The AI does not make purchases on the user’s behalf, and the final decision always belongs to the user.

Seven specialist advisors are live, covering categories that include investment guidance, travel, cars, film, health information, music, and real estate. The project’s aim is to make AI useful in everyday purchasing decisions by helping people move from describing a need to identifying a relevant option.

Businesses can also submit products and services to the network. This approach is designed to connect consumers with suitable offers while giving participating businesses another way to reach potential customers.

Its public development tracker is updated as progress happens and identifies current work on partner listings, advisor improvements, and payment functionality. The project plans to begin its first partner payments in $CON in February 2027.

The project says each listing will be announced once confirmed. These are plans, not confirmed listing agreements, and should not be treated as guaranteed dates or outcomes.

The MEXC listing is currently on hold because of the exchange’s regulatory situation. Its liquidity position is reported to be locked with UNCX until November 6, 2028. The project says pool fees currently help cover development and marketing costs, with partner payments expected to contribute once the listings platform opens.

ConConAI reports that the live $CON contract audit has been completed. It also cites a TokenSniffer score of 100/100, contract verification on Etherscan, and listings on CoinMarketCap, CoinGecko, DEXTools, and DexScreener. These are useful verification and discovery signals, but they do not eliminate market, smart-contract or third-party platform risks.

The project’s transparency page provides live wallet balances and burn records. Its published allocation includes 30 million $CON for the community, 15 million for liquidity, 10 million for centralized-exchange liquidity, and approximately 5 million for project purposes. The project says its allocation wallets use Safe multisig arrangements. The official contract address is 0x7ad1A8Fc42Ac150B04dED5825D21a0C90b6d28D8.

$CON’s early market performance has given ConConAI a strong starting point following its Uniswap debut. Its ability to maintain interest will increasingly depend on trading participation, liquidity, product delivery, and the development of real commercial activity around its AI advisors.

If the project converts its existing development progress into wider consumer adoption and partner participation, the token’s intended utility could become an increasingly important part of its market proposition. Combined with the reported supply reduction and community-led roadmap, these factors provide a positive basis for watching $CON’s next phase, while recognising the volatility and risks associated with newly launched crypto assets.

ConConAI is developing a network of AI-powered personal purchase advisors and commercial partner listings. Its $CON token is intended to support partner activity across the ecosystem, including listings, placements, and performance-based fees.

#5130. Ethereum’s Co-Founder Takes On Crypto’s Next Security Threat. Who Is Vitalik Buterin?

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Who is Vitalik Buterin, and why is Ethereum’s co-founder now questioning the security of the very devices crypto investors use to protect their wealth? The 32-year-old programmer has turned his attention to a problem that even open-source software cannot necessarily solve: compromised computer chips.

In an essay published on November 26, Buterin argued that cryptocurrency security needs to extend beyond software and into the physical hardware on which it runs. His message builds on one of crypto’s oldest principles, but with a new twist:

For someone who helped build an alternative to centralized financial infrastructure, questioning the manufacturers behind that infrastructure seems like a natural next step.

Vitalik Buterin is a Russian-Canadian programmer, researcher and writer who conceived Ethereum in 2013, at the age of 19.

Born in Russia in 1994 and raised in Canada, Buterin discovered Bitcoin in 2011. He went on to co-found Bitcoin Magazine, where he explored the technology and economics behind cryptocurrencies long before digital assets attracted mainstream financial institutions.

His involvement in Bitcoin exposed him to a problem that would eventually lead to Ethereum. Blockchain technology had potential beyond transferring money, but building more sophisticated applications on Bitcoin presented technical limitations.

Rather than trying to accommodate every possible application within Bitcoin’s existing architecture, Buterin began working on a blockchain designed specifically for programmability.

At the time, he was studying computer science at the University of Waterloo, where he also worked as a research assistant to cryptographer Ian Goldberg.

According to the University of Waterloo, Buterin received a $100,000 Thiel Fellowship in 2014 and subsequently left university to work on Ethereum full-time.

In November 2013, Buterin wrote the initial draft of what would become the Ethereum whitepaper.

The proposal described a blockchain with a general-purpose programming environment. Developers would no longer need to create an entirely new network every time they wanted to build a decentralized application.

Consider a lending platform. Instead of relying on a bank to manage collateral, calculate interest and authorize withdrawals, developers could encode those rules into smart contracts running on Ethereum.

That does not eliminate every risk. Smart contracts can contain bugs, depend on unreliable external data or operate under centralized administrative controls. What Ethereum introduced was the ability to execute financial and other programmable agreements on a shared blockchain.

Although Buterin originated the concept, Ethereum was not built by him alone. Its founding team included seven other individuals: Gavin Wood, Joseph Lubin, Charles Hoskinson, Anthony Di Iorio, Mihai Alisie, Jeffrey Wilcke and Amir Chetrit.

The project’s first live network, known as Frontier, launched on July 30, 2015.

What began as an experimental computing platform eventually became the foundation for much of the decentralized finance industry. Stablecoins, decentralized exchanges, lending protocols and tokenized financial assets now use the infrastructure that Buterin and Ethereum’s early contributors helped establish.

The network’s own evolution, particularly its transition to proof-of-stake and the development of Layer 2 scaling networks, has shaped Ethereum’s first decade.

A hardware wallet is supposed to keep private keys away from potentially compromised computers and smartphones. But what happens if the device itself cannot be trusted?

Buterin’s latest research examines that possibility. He points to supply chain attacks involving tampered wallets and considers the potential for malicious modifications concealed inside apparently legitimate chips.

Open-source firmware allows researchers to examine the instructions a device runs. But those instructions reveal little about whether the manufactured chip has been altered.

Buterin wants manufacturers to disclose physical chip layouts, known as GDS files, so investigators have a reference against which to inspect actual hardware.

The distinction matters. Knowing what a chip is designed to do is not necessarily the same as knowing what the chip inside your wallet actually does.

One approach highlighted by Buterin comes from hardware security researcher Andrew Huang, better known as bunnie.

Huang has been developing a technique called Infra-Red, In Situ inspection (IRIS), which exploits the fact that silicon becomes transparent at certain infrared wavelengths.

Using infrared illumination and suitable imaging equipment, researchers can examine parts of a chip’s internal structure without necessarily removing it from its circuit board.

The technique could help detect substituted components or unexpected differences between manufactured chips and their intended designs.

In a 2024 update on his research, Huang explained that infrared imaging has resolution limits. It cannot reliably reveal every microscopic feature of modern chips. Combining imaging with additional electrical testing could improve confidence in a component’s integrity.

That is an important limitation for crypto investors. Publishing an open hardware design does not automatically make a wallet secure, just as publishing a smart contract’s code does not establish that it is free of vulnerabilities.

Buterin acknowledges that sophisticated hardware inspections are more likely to be performed by specialist organizations than ordinary wallet owners.

His essay is a proposal for improving security, not an announcement that existing hardware wallets have all been compromised.

Despite his status as Ethereum’s most recognizable co-founder, Buterin is not its CEO.

Ethereum is maintained through the participation of independent developers, researchers, node operators, validators and other ecosystem contributors. Changes to the network involve technical proposals, discussion, software development and adoption by participants.

Buterin has considerable influence over those discussions, but publishing a proposal does not give him the authority to implement it unilaterally.

His role within the Ethereum Foundation is also distinct from control over the blockchain itself. In its April 2025 governance announcement, the Foundation described Buterin’s responsibilities as providing technical and intellectual guidance to the wider ecosystem.

His research can influence the direction Ethereum takes. Whether the network ultimately follows that direction depends on considerably more than his endorsement.

Buterin accumulated considerable wealth through his involvement in Ethereum, with much of his publicly visible cryptocurrency wealth tied to ETH.

However, his exact net worth is not publicly established.

Blockchain analytics can estimate the value of assets held in wallets attributed to him, but those figures do not necessarily account for all his investments, liabilities, private assets or holdings at addresses that have not been publicly identified.

They also fluctuate with cryptocurrency prices. A wallet valuation should therefore not be confused with a complete assessment of his personal wealth.

Buterin’s latest essay is part of a longer-running interest in making digital infrastructure independently verifiable.

In September 2025, he published The Importance of Full-Stack Openness and Verifiability, exploring how transparency could extend across the hardware and software underpinning increasingly important parts of people’s lives.

These interests share a practical concern: whether users can independently establish that the systems they rely on behave as intended.

There is a commercial obstacle, though. Semiconductor manufacturers invest heavily in proprietary processes, and designing chips specifically for inspectability can involve performance compromises.

But a device signing a cryptocurrency transaction does not necessarily need the computing power of a modern AI processor. That makes security-focused hardware a potentially useful starting point.

More than a decade ago, Buterin challenged the idea that blockchains should primarily be used to transfer money. His latest work challenges another assumption the industry has grown comfortable with: that trusting the code is enough.

For crypto investors, the next meaningful development may come from hardware manufacturers willing to make their products independently inspectable, rather than another software update promising greater security.
