#5129. Ripple News: XRP Price Tries to Reclaim $1 Again – But Will The Breakout Survive the Weekend?

Ripple news: XRP climbs 3.6% toward $1 as RLUSD hits a record supply and ETF inflows return. Can XRP finally break resistance?

XRP is approaching a price level it has repeatedly failed to reclaim. According to the latest Ripple news, the token climbed 3.6% to $0.978 on November 27, putting $1 back within reach for the sixth time in two weeks.

The token has a busy week of Ripple updates behind it. Ripple signed a Turkish bank as a custody client, and its RLUSD stablecoin reached a record supply. Spot XRP ETFs, which hold the token itself, drew fresh money. XRP Ledger validators also moved closer to switching on a lending feature.

JUST IN: Ripple’s lending proposal is one validator vote from $XRP Ledger approval, potentially unlocking lending for its $837 million stablecoin market. pic.twitter.com/jB5a4RYAlK

— Whale Insider (@WhaleInsider) November 27, 2026

XRP needs the help. It is down 56% from a year ago and has lost more than a fifth of its value since the start of November.

The question is whether this Ripple news is enough to push XRP back through $1. Our check of the daily chart shows why the level matters so much.

The largest piece of Ripple news came on Wednesday. Ripple announced that Yapı Kredi, one of Türkiye’s largest private banks, will use Ripple Custody to hold crypto for its trading arm. The system runs on the bank’s own premises. Ripple says its technology now sits behind every leading Turkish bank licensed as a crypto custodian, and that the company holds more than 85 licenses worldwide.

Ripple’s stablecoin is growing too. RLUSD’s supply reached a record of about $2.85 billion this week across Ethereum and the XRP Ledger, making it the fifth-largest stablecoin.

Fund demand is returning, slowly. US spot XRP ETFs took in $4.07 million on Tuesday, the only crypto ETF group with inflows that day. The five funds hold $1.04 billion in total, though they are still $21 million in the red over the past 30 days.

On the XRP Ledger, the network that XRP runs on, validators are close to approving a bank-style lending system. A vault feature could go live on December 9. The lending upgrade, which validators must vote on, is one vote short of the support it needs.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Next Crypto to Hit 1 Dollar

To see why $1 matters, we went through XRP’s daily candles on Binance since June.

The level held XRP up for most of the summer. XRP touched $1 in late June and again for two weeks in August, and buyers stepped in each time. After a brief dip in mid-August, it then closed above $1 for 89 days in a row, from August 17 to November 13.

That streak ended on November 14, when XRP fell 10% in a day. Since then the old floor has acted as a ceiling. XRP’s daily high reached or came within a cent of $1 on November 14, 17, 18, 19 and 23, and every time sellers pushed it back. The highest attempt, on Monday, briefly hit $1.026 before XRP closed at $0.94.

Binance’s order book shows the wall too. On Friday afternoon, sell orders worth about $700,000 sat at $1.00, more than double the orders at $0.99.

EXPLORE: Ripple Lands Major Turkish Bank Deal – So Why is XRP/Lira Trading Down 70%?

XRP trades at $0.978, below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $1.13, and its 200-day EMA at $1.29.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Reveals Upcoming Coinbase Listings

This week’s Ripple news gives XRP more reasons to rally than it had a month ago. But the chart has the final say, and the first daily close above $1 since November 13 is the signal to wait for.

#5127. ‘Most bearish thing for XMR’ — What KuCoin’s Monero delisting means for liquidity

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

KuCoin is in the news today after announcing that it would remove Monero [XMR] spot trading on 30th November. The exchange’s XMR/USDT and XMR/USDC pairs accounted for over half of Monero’s spot trading volume on CoinGecko.

With such a large trading venue leaving, where would Monero traders go next?

KuCoin has scheduled the removal of XMR/USDT, XMR/USDC, XMR/ETH and XMR/BTC for 08:00 UTC on 30th November. Deposits have already been closed permanently too.

Withdrawals will close at 08:00 UTC on 31st December 2026. KuCoin reserves the right to close them earlier over project-related issues, with the exchange also warning that stablecoin conversion of remaining balances won’t be guaranteed.

At press time, CoinGecko highlighted $90.42 million in combined 24-hour volumes across KuCoin’s XMR/USDT and XMR/USDC pairs. Together, they accounted for 50.27% of Monero’s spot trading volume.

Including XMR/BTC and XMR/ETH, that brought KuCoin’s total to $104.60 million or 58.14%.

Hence, the question: Where could that trading move now? At the time of writing, the remaining exchanges showed more buy orders close to the market price, despite reporting a lower turnover.

Kraken’s XMR/USD pair had approximately $386,970 in buy orders within 2% below its price, compared to KuCoin’s XMR/USDT pair’s $85,683. WhiteBIT and HTX’s XMR/USDT pairs showed $260,810 and $196,231, respectively.

That gave Kraken roughly 4.5 times KuCoin’s nearby buying depth, with WhiteBIT and HTX also offering larger buy-side cushions. These orders could help absorb selling, although traders could cancel them at any time.

That access problem extended into services marketed as alternatives to CEXs.

X user and the founder of XMRHub called KuCoin’s delisting “the most bearish thing for $XMR.” According to the exec, the exchange supported swap services, liquidity, and onboarding.

Another X user, PerpetualCow, described the alleged connection more directly. He said,

Instant swap exchanges don’t have their own liquidity, they simply wrapped around Kucoin and sold/bought into their order books.

Still, the proposed dependency might explain why another exchange closure could affect apparently separate services. Swap interface routing orders through KuCoin would need another supplier, sufficient inventory, or a different execution route.

Dash’s Joel Valenzuela also raised a similar concern. He warned that further CEX losses could make no-KYC Monero swaps harder to obtain.

Finally, Cake Wallet founder Vik Sharma also directed users towards wallet-based swaps, writing,

Why does Monero keep getting delisted? Because it works!

The announcement followed another loss of exchange access earlier that month. MEXC ended XMR spot trading on 17th November. Its XMR Perpetual Futures closed separately on 13th November.

Kraken, for its part, had been explicit about its own rationale. It cited regulatory changes when halting XMR trading and deposits for European Economic Area customers on 31st October 2024.

#5125. Zcash Developers Race to Secure Crypto. Can Quantum Computing Break Bitcoin?

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Can quantum computing break crypto? For years, the question has largely been treated as a problem for the distant future. Zcash developers, however, are already discussing what to do with hundreds of thousands of coins that could become vulnerable if certain cryptographic protections fail.

A day earlier, Shielded Labs published its first technical update on a separate project designed to protect Zcash against future quantum computers.

Neither development means cryptocurrency has been cracked. Together, however, they raise a more pressing question: can blockchain developers replace the mathematics protecting investors’ money before someone finds a way around it?

Quantum computing is a way of processing information using the properties of quantum mechanics. Unlike conventional computers, which represent information using bits with a value of either zero or one, quantum computers operate using quantum bits, commonly known as qubits.

By manipulating these qubits, researchers can design algorithms capable of solving certain mathematical problems far more efficiently than conventional computers.

The important word here is certain. A quantum computer is not simply a faster version of the laptop sitting on your desk. Its advantages depend on the type of problem it is trying to solve.

Unfortunately for the cryptocurrency industry, some of those problems underpin the security of digital wallets.

As explained in NewsBTC’s guide to quantum computing, blockchains rely on cryptographic signatures to establish ownership and authorize transactions. A sufficiently powerful quantum computer could undermine some of the signature systems currently used to protect digital assets.

When you send Bitcoin from your wallet, the network needs to establish that you have the authority to spend those coins. It does this by verifying a digital signature produced using your private key.

Your private key is supposed to remain secret. The corresponding public key can be disclosed because working backward from a public key to its private counterpart is computationally impractical using conventional methods.

In 1994, mathematician Peter Shor introduced a quantum algorithm that could efficiently solve certain mathematical problems underlying modern public-key cryptography.

A sufficiently powerful quantum computer running such an algorithm could potentially recover private keys from exposed public keys. An attacker could then create a transaction that the blockchain would recognize as valid, even though the original owner had never authorized it.

That is a particularly uncomfortable problem for cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin does not have a customer service department that can reverse an unauthorized transfer.

The National Institute of Standards and Technology has already developed alternative cryptographic standards intended to withstand these future attacks. The challenge for crypto is incorporating such protection into networks that were originally built around different assumptions.

Bitcoin’s public transaction history makes it possible to estimate how much of its supply could be exposed under certain quantum attack scenarios.

According to a November 25 snapshot from The Quantum Ledger, approximately 7.23 million BTC, representing 35.9% of issued supply under its methodology, was associated with public keys or spending scripts already visible on the blockchain.

Around 1.94 million BTC was classified as exposed because of its output design. A further 5.29 million BTC was associated with addresses that had previously revealed relevant spending information.

Some of these coins date back to Bitcoin’s earliest years, when transactions commonly revealed public keys directly.

Estimates vary between researchers because they do not all measure exposure in exactly the same way. In May 2026, Glassnode’s research identified 6.04 million BTC under its own classification framework.

These figures should not be interpreted as the amount of Bitcoin that will eventually be stolen. They measure a potential vulnerability under a specific future scenario, not an active attack.

Owners of many exposed coins could migrate their holdings if suitable protection becomes available. Dormant wallets whose owners have lost their private keys present a considerably harder problem.

Zcash offers a useful example of how complicated a cryptographic migration can become.

Sapling is one of the network’s older shielded systems. Its proof mechanism relies on mathematical assumptions that Zakura believes warrant additional scrutiny in light of potentially accelerating cryptographic research.

The time to prepare for a cryptographic breakthrough is before it happens.

The amount involved is already changing. A November 27 snapshot from the Zcash Dashboard, timestamped 06:06 UTC, showed approximately 306,684 ZEC remaining in Sapling, below the rounded estimate cited in Zakura’s proposal. The difference does not, by itself, establish that the warning prompted users to move their funds.

The discussion follows Zcash’s recent NU7 network upgrade, which improved transaction speed and continued the network’s transition away from older infrastructure.

Importantly, the immediate concern raised by Zakura is not evidence of a successful quantum attack. It relates to speculative advances in mathematics that could affect particular cryptographic constructions. Those advances remain unverified.

One of the problems its researchers are working on is the size of cryptographic proofs.

Stronger protection can require considerably more data to be processed and transmitted. That can create difficulties for blockchains, where transaction capacity, verification costs and storage requirements already matter.

The team is evaluating two possible approaches and expects to select a direction by the end of January 2027, provided its research progresses as planned.

Ironwood already incorporates features intended to support a future recovery mechanism. However, the developers have made clear that these features do not make Zcash fully quantum-resistant today.

The distinction is important. Having a contingency plan for a future attack is not the same as having protection against one.

Zcash is not the only network confronting these issues.

Bitcoin developers are discussing changes through proposals including BIP-360, which would introduce a transaction output format designed to reduce certain forms of public-key exposure.

A separate draft, BIP-361, explores a gradual transition away from vulnerable signature schemes once suitable alternatives are available.

Neither proposal should be confused with an activated Bitcoin upgrade.

Ethereum faces additional complications. Beyond individual wallets, its security model relies on cryptographic signatures used by validators and other infrastructure.

Ethereum’s quantum-security challenge extends to staking arrangements and institutional custody.

There is also a governance problem that applies particularly to Bitcoin. If millions of coins remain in old wallets that cannot be migrated, should the network eventually restrict their movement to prevent potential theft?

Doing so could protect the broader ecosystem, but it could also prevent legitimate owners from accessing their own money. Leaving those coins untouched carries a different set of risks.

Cryptography alone cannot settle that argument.

There is no reliable date for when a quantum computer capable of breaking widely used cryptocurrency signatures will become available.

Building such a machine requires more than increasing the number of qubits. Those qubits must also be reliable enough to carry out lengthy, complex calculations without errors overwhelming the results.

According to Coinbase Institute’s research, the relevant machines do not yet exist, but the process of upgrading blockchains, wallets and custody infrastructure could itself take years.

For that reason, waiting for an actual attack before implementing stronger cryptography would be a risky approach.

Crypto investors should pay attention to what developers implement, whether wallets support the new protections and whether existing funds can be migrated without compromising ownership.

There is no need to buy a token simply because its developers describe it as quantum-resistant, either. Such claims deserve scrutiny of the underlying cryptography and its implementation.

Zcash’s latest proposals offer a glimpse of the decisions other blockchain communities may eventually face. Replacing an algorithm is one thing. Persuading an entire decentralized financial network to move its money before a deadline is something else entirely.

Bitcoin has joined a broader rebound in risk assets as US markets reopen for a shortened session after Thanksgiving. The top cryptocurrency has risen about 1.8% so far today and is trading near $61,600, putting it on course to snap seven straight weekly losses if the gain holds through Sunday. Stocks have led the move, with Nasdaq-100 futures up more than 2%, while silver has jumped around 7% and gold has added roughly 2.5%.

The recovery follows a difficult stretch, as Bitcoin still remains down over 20% in November (its largest monthly decline since June), and US spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded monthly outflows of $5.39 billion. The Fear and Greed Index sits at 11, signaling extreme fear, and roughly $7 billion in Bitcoin options expired earlier today with traders positioned defensively. Total crypto market capitalization stands near $2.1 trillion, up 1.09% on the day, with Bitcoin’s own market cap at $1.23 trillion.

While prices stabilize and caution lingers, the BTC Layer 2 project Bitcoin Hyper (HYPER) has closed its presale, which raised $33.3 million since it began in May last year. Participants are now able to claim their HYPER tokens, which can also be traded on the top DEX platforms Uniswap and Raydium. Bitcoin Hyper’s strong raise and timely token generation event highlight sustained interest in infrastructure that can expand Bitcoin’s practical uses, setting the stage for the project’s next development steps.

Bitcoin Hyper (HYPER) is aiming to be the fastest true Bitcoin Layer 2 network. It integrates the Solana Virtual Machine to deliver high throughput and low latency, allowing near-instant Bitcoin transactions at minimal cost while settling security back to Bitcoin’s Layer 1. Users deposit native BTC into a Canonical Bridge, which verifies Bitcoin block headers and transaction proofs before minting equivalent wrapped BTC on the Layer 2.

That wrapped BTC can then move freely for payments, decentralized finance activity, staking, and on-chain applications. Withdrawals reverse the process, returning BTC to the user’s Layer 1 address after state verification.

The HYPER token functions as the network’s native utility asset. It covers gas fees for transfers and smart-contract interactions, supports staking for rewards, and grants access to advanced features and governance participation. Token allocations direct 20% to marketing, 15% to rewards, 30% to development, 25% to the project’s treasury, and 10% to major exchange listings.

Hyper Mainnet is now secured by @hackenclub 🔓 ⚡

Final Report: https://t.co/nSJy3Ys8mY pic.twitter.com/zY1ahvp7dQ

— Bitcoin Hyper (@BTC_Hyper2) November 26, 2026

The Bitcoin Hyper network’s architecture relies on a hybrid design (audited by Hacken), in which the Layer 2 handles execution via the Solana Virtual Machine and a Proof-of-Stake validator set, while Bitcoin’s Proof-of-Work system provides periodic anchoring for state integrity.

The completed HYPER presale, which drew $33.3 million, shows clear demand for these capabilities. With the token generation event now finished, buyers can access their allocations as the project moves forward with its Layer 2 deployment timeline.

The Bitcoin Hyper claiming process begins on the project’s official website. Users should first hard-refresh the page to clear the cache, then connect the same wallet employed during the presale. Two options will be available: a standard claim or a claim-and-stake choice.

Solana purchases will need to be claimed on Solana with the original wallet; Ethereum, BSC, or credit-card purchases can be claimed only on Ethereum. Credit card buyers can locate the registered wallet address on their Wert receipt.

Best Wallet holders can claim directly through the app’s Upcoming Tokens section; mobile users should also get smoother results by opening the site inside the wallet’s built-in browser. The project recommends keeping $10–20 worth of ETH or SOL on hand for gas fees incurred during the claim process.

The team will never request private keys or seed phrases, and claims can be completed only through the official site or through Best Wallet. A full guide to claiming HYPER has been published on X via the official Bitcoin Hyper account.

Full claim instructions on the official Hyper TG 👇https://t.co/iukXzZWfcX pic.twitter.com/6SneDFHPBO

— Bitcoin Hyper (@BTC_Hyper2) November 26, 2026

HYPER is available for trading on Uniswap and Raydium. Staked tokens become claimable starting December 3, and any tokens staked after the presale ends will be claimable exactly seven days later. The project is continuing its progress toward the Layer 2 mainnet launch on December 3, when staked allocations unlock and additional network components go live.

This sequence keeps Bitcoin Hyper on track to broaden Bitcoin’s utility through faster settlement and expanded application support, reinforcing a positive outlook for the token as the leading cryptocurrency’s everyday functionality expands.

#5122. Cardano’s Next Chapter: Euler Named as Major Upgrade After Dijkstra

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Cardano is already looking beyond its upcoming Dijkstra hard fork, with Euler emerging as the next major upgrade.

In a recent release, Intersect, a member-based organization in the Cardano ecosystem, said it is planning the next Cardano upgrade, Euler, with the first meeting of the Euler Scoping Working Group scheduled for December 1, 2026, at 5 p.m. UTC. Here, participants will contribute to early discussions on the scope of the next Cardano era.

The development signals Cardano's continued commitment to evolving its blockchain infrastructure through a structured upgrade process. While Dijkstra represents the current focus, discussions on Euler will set the tone for what comes next for the network.

The Dijkstra era delivers Cardano's major protocol upgrade in two phases: Phase 1, Dijkstra hard fork (Protocol Version 12), introduces the Dijkstra ledger era and ships Ouroboros Linear Leios as a complete, activated feature. The second phase activates Ouroboros Peras via an intra-era hard fork. Peras is a settlement-speed upgrade that adds a voting overlay to the existing Ouroboros Praos chain selection rule.

As of the latest update by Intersect, Dijkstra ledger features are currently being tested on DijkstraNet, while Linear Leios consensus and throughput are being tested on MusashiNet. Both are converging toward Node 11.3, which is the target hard fork release candidate.

The Dijkstra upgrade requires both constitutional and technical changes in the era of on-chain governance. Discussions and refinements on constitutional guardrails (Update Constitution) or CAP-12 "Dijkstra era parameters" continue on the Constitutional Amendment Portal ahead of Mainnet submission.

Protocol Version 12 has already gone live on Musashi and DijkstraNet, while a hard fork release candidate (11.3) is required for Preview and Preprod hard forks. In its recent post, Intersect sets the Dijkstra hard fork target timeline as December 2026 for the Preview network, including the Update Constitution and hard fork.

On-chain activation of the Update Constitution action on the mainnet is expected in December 2026, while the Dijkstra hard fork is expected in Q1 2027.

Crypto traders who bet on a decline lost nearly $170 million to liquidations over the past 24 hours as Bitcoin, Solana and XRP rose on Black Friday. Short positions made up 68.3% of the $248.8 million in total liquidations.

CoinGlass data showed on Friday that liquidations hit 72,023 traders over that period, and Binance accounted for 44.9% of the total. The largest single order was a $9.3 million BTCUSDT short on Binance, which CoinGlass recorded at a price of $62,147.

Bitcoin shorts lost $64.9 million over 24 hours, and Bitcoin longs lost $20.9 million, according to CoinGlass. On the CoinGlass heatmap, shorts made up 75.7% of Bitcoin's $85.8 million in liquidations across all trading pairs. Bitcoin was trading at around $61,400 on Friday, up 0.9% over 24 hours.

CoinGlass recorded $139.6 million of the short liquidations in the past 12 hours, against $29.9 million in long liquidations over the same window.

Ethereum shorts lost $38.1 million, the second-largest amount among all assets on CoinGlass. ETH traded at around $1,721 on Friday, up 1% over 24 hours.

According to CoinGlass, Solana gained 3.3% to around $73, and SOL shorts lost $6 million. XRP rose 1.9% to $0.97, and its shorts lost $2 million.

On Thursday, CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju estimated in a post on X that Bitcoin had about $16 billion in potential short liquidations between $60,000 and $100,000. According to Ju, potential long liquidations below that range totaled less than $5 billion. "The squeeze risk is on the short side," he wrote.

Deribit's monthly Bitcoin options expiry took place at 08:00 UTC on Friday. About 110,800 BTC contracts, worth roughly $6.75 billion, expired with a max pain price of $70,000, according to Deribit data.

BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes warned about the weekend in an X post on Friday. "If there is no Fed dovish rhetoric pivot before the pre-FOMC blackout begins EOD Fri US time, this weekend could get spicy," Hayes wrote. He added that liquid assets and crypto could get dumped before Monday's open.

Earlier this week, Hayes said that Bitcoin "will retest $55k" and shared a chart with the price at $58,773. On Nov. 21, Bitcoin fell as low as $55,150, its lowest price since September 2024.

At its October meeting, the Fed held its benchmark rate at 3.75%–4% in a 10–2 vote. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack voted for a quarter-point hike.

The Fed's blackout period starts at midnight ET on Nov. 28, and the FOMC will announce its rate decision on Dec. 9. CME FedWatch put the odds of a 25-basis-point hike at 100% on Nov. 12.

#5119. XRP Updates: The Ambitious Projects That Contribute to Its Widespread Adoption

XRP has earned a reputation as one of the fastest and lowest-cost cryptocurrencies for payments, powered by the XRP Ledger. The Ripple company, under which both technologies thrive, has positioned itself as a tool for companies that want to modernize their infrastructure and approach decentralization effortlessly. The platform supports more than 1,000,000 custody wallets, enabling […]

XRP has earned a reputation as one of the fastest and lowest-cost cryptocurrencies for payments, powered by the XRP Ledger. The Ripple company, under which both technologies thrive, has positioned itself as a tool for companies that want to modernize their infrastructure and approach decentralization effortlessly.

The platform supports more than 1,000,000 custody wallets, enabling users to settle in 3 to 5 seconds. Crypto businesses, payment services providers, and FinTechs can leverage Ripple’s payment system, so use cases are numerous and convincing for investors to buy XRP.

The popularity and growing interest have contributed to the project’s expansion, including securing additional licenses, extending its escrow functionality, and exploring the possibility of native XRP staking, according to the latest news. A lot is going on in the Ripple ecosystem, so let’s explore more about these additions.

The ledger is known for its high performance, low cost, and appeal for streamlined development, making it the perfect option for business use. That’s what the latest upgrade is about, the “Permissioned DEX”. According to the project documentation, the upgrade will allow regulated institutions to manage traded venues on-chain or benefit from a controlled version of the XRPL decentralized exchange.

The supposed administrators of the venues can delegate trades by checking who can place and accept them, which supports a members-only marketplace for different organizations. This will be possible in accordance with compliance requirements, including KYC (Know Your Customer) and AML (Anti-Money Laundering) procedures.

The benefits of this update include increased liquidity and a blockchain-based settlement system, enabling companies to better manage counterparty eligibility. Moreover, users can benefit from the ledgers’ security, but access to information will be restricted accordingly.

When it comes to official banks using XRP, the EU isn’t necessarily the leading region; Asia-Pacific is the leading region. However, this will change soon, as Ripple has received an important approval from the UK’s Financial Conduct Authority for its EMI (Electronic Money Institution) license.

The announcement was soon followed by another approval by Luxembourg’s financial regulator, CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier). Both regulations strengthen Ripple’s trust across Europe by demonstrating the company’s willingness to operate in accordance with comprehensive digital asset regulations.

Ripple has expanded its regulatory footprint to over 75 licenses globally, and the platform now supports more than 90% of daily foreign exchange markets. Therefore, it is ready to lead the global industry into the next era of financial innovation by securing both compliant operations and advanced technologies such as blockchain.

Hyperliquid is one of the fastest-growing decentralized exchanges, with its own blockchain and specializing in perpetual futures trading. Its low fees, favorable leverage levels, and a vast array of assets have made the decentralized exchange an innovative tool in the industry, and Ripple eyed its potential for collaboration.

By integrating Hyperliquid into its prime brokerage platform, Ripple offered institutional customers the chance to leverage on-chain derivatives liquidity while accessing numerous asset classes, from crypto to foreign exchange. The efforts mark the start of a new trend that addresses decentralized exchanges supporting all sorts of assets.

Of course, the collaboration increased the value of Hyperliquid’s native token, HYPE, making it more efficient for users to transact on the blockchain. However, XRP also saw a boost in value following the announcement, showcasing the power of industry collaborations.

The native token of XRPL has seen considerable appreciation for its transaction benefits, but its journey has also faced challenges. Ripple’s court case with the SEC left a question mark regarding the company’s commitment to the global business sector, despite Ripple’s victory after five years of proceedings.

The SEC accused Ripple of facilitating the sale of unregistered securities, which sparked endless disputes over what cryptocurrencies truly are and what the SEC’s stance is on crypto technology. XRP also saw lower prices during this period due to reduced interest in a company facing court cases. In the meantime, the SEC’s management also changed with a more crypto-oriented approach.

Besides these issues, Ripple has continued to expand and is thriving, leading us to believe the future will follow a similar path. Considering the growing number of collaborations with other industry companies and the interest in advanced technological tooling, Ripple might become a competitive brand in the future of Web3.

While the price of XRP still hasn’t reached the heights of Bitcoin or Ethereum, it still has the potential to be useful for real-world cases. As one of the largest coins by market capitalization, XRP is slowly but steadily being adopted by brands that want to offer users the option to pay with crypto, especially since it operates at fast speeds and low fees.

Therefore, XRP is a suitable investment for a diversified portfolio, as it’s supported by active real-world integration and a global user base. As experts forecast rising prices and expanded adoption in the future, investing in it can help build a stable, reliable long-term portfolio.

For those who don’t want to buy the actual coin and only benefit from exposure, they can invest in XRP ETFs, as several SEC-approved ETFs are available on the market from Grayscale or 21Shares. Each listing has different fees, but they may change. In addition, more XRP ETFs will launch in the future as new funds are launched.

XRP is one of the most controversial cryptocurrencies due to its court case with the SEC, but this hasn’t fully affected the brand and its efficiency. Following the victory over the SEC, XRP continued to expand its use cases and collaborations to better support future adoption. For example, some of the latest additions to the Ripple ecosystem include new regulations in the EU and a partnership with a decentralized exchange.

#5116. Ethereum: Glamsterdam on the way after devs schedule Hoodi testnet run for December 15

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Ethereum developers have agreed to move ahead with the next step in the Glamsterdam upgrade.

The key takeaway? Reaching consensus was not easy. Developers flagged potential network disruptions and usability issues with the new gas opcode. Still, they decided to proceed with it. In fact, the team also agreed to schedule the Hoodi testnet upgrade for 15th December at 7:12 PM UTC, moving Glamsterdam testing closer to implementation. So, what does this tell us?

As highlighted in the developer’ discussion, Ethereum is emphasizing post-quantum security within its development, in addition to focusing on on-chain enhancements. Simply put, regardless of the ongoing concerns, the developers are clearly moving away from just looking at scaling and speed, and towards ensuring Ethereum is future-proof in relation to quantum computing.

The meeting focused on deciding the scope and timing of the Glamsterdam upgrade and the prioritization of post-quantum security features. The execution layer teams reached a rough consensus to proceed with the current Glamsterdam spec as is, with the Hoodi testnet upgrade scheduled for December 15 at 7:12 PM UTC.

Interestingly, this was also reflected in the debate around the upcoming Heze upgrade.

There was debate about whether to support Fossil or to place a bigger emphasis on post-quantum work. Concern was expressed that Fossil may also require development effort. Though no conclusion was reached, the matter will be discussed further at the next team meeting. Meanwhile, Kevaundray suggested that Keccak256 should be used as the hashing algorithm for Ethereum’s post-quantum work.

Against this backdrop, the Heze upgrade moving forward does not seem far-fetched. With the Hoodi upgrade scheduled and Keccak256 proposed for post-quantum security, Ethereum’s [ETH] focus on strengthening its long-term security is now becoming clearer.

The Hoodi testnet is a testing version of Ethereum that allows developers to trial upcoming upgrades.

Think of it as a testing ground where developers can identify bugs and ensure upgrades like Glamsterdam work smoothly before reaching Ethereum users. Within the wider scope of Ethereum’s post-quantum development, it may also be used to test new security features, again allowing developers to analyze how prepared they are to then apply these to the mainnet.

That makes Hoodi an important test for Glamsterdam, giving developers a clearer picture of whether the upgrade is ready for mainnet. Why does this matter? Well, Glamsterdam aims to improve transaction processing. If successful, these changes could strengthen Ethereum’s network fundamentals. Here, the timing matters too.

As the chart shows, Ethereum has processed just over 100 million transactions in Q4 so far. By comparison, the network averaged more than 200 million transactions per quarter in 2026. This puts Q4 activity well below its recent pace, with ETH’s technical structure also showing signs of weakness.

Against this backdrop, the Hoodi testnet upgrade could mark an important inflection point for Ethereum.

A successful rollout would bring Glamsterdam closer to mainnet deployment. In turn, the upgrade could boost Ethereum’s throughput, improve execution efficiency, and support stronger on-chain activity.

Ethereum developers are moving ahead with Glamsterdam while focusing more on future quantum security.

The Hoodi testnet will help test the upgrade before mainnet, with the goal of making Ethereum faster and more efficient.

Bitcoin's 90-day correlation with gold has reached its highest level on record, according to Galaxy Research data. The measure peaked at 0.56 on Oct. 22 and broke the previous record of 0.50, which Galaxy dated to Nov. 6, 2020.

Alex Thorn, head of firmwide research at Galaxy Digital, posted about the record on X on Friday. "Bitcoin isn't digital gold? Bitcoin reaches highest correlation to gold of all time," he wrote.

Thorn shared two Galaxy Research charts together with the post. According to the charts, the 90-day correlation was at 0.54 on Nov. 23, and the 30-day correlation stood at 0.59 on the same day.

In the first half of 2026, the 90-day correlation stayed near 0.1. It started to rise in July and climbed above 0.50 by early October, according to Galaxy's data. Between 2020 and 2025, the average reading was 0.11.

On Jan. 20, Galaxy CEO Mike Novogratz wrote on X that "the gold price is telling us we are losing reserve currency status at an accelerating rate." "$BTC is disappointing as it is still being met with selling," he added.

Thorn wrote about Bitcoin and gold on X in February. "Bitcoin's failure to trade like gold as part of 'the debasement trade' since Sep. '25 damaged its narrative with new entrants," he wrote. "When bitcoiners said 'digital gold,' they were describing its fundamental properties, not that it's high beta to gold today," he added.

On Wednesday, Galaxy published a report that withdrew its Oct. 26 call on the Bitcoin bear market. "We withdraw our call that the bear market ended in June," the report said. Thorn shared it on X with the comment, "As it turns out, the Bitcoin bear market is definitely not over."

According to the report, Bitcoin closed the week ended Nov. 22 at $61,104 after seven straight weekly losses. Thorn wrote in the report that the level to watch was $58,525, Bitcoin's closing low from June 30. According to Thorn, a daily close below that level would mark "the start of a move to a materially lower low."

"The clock says this bear is overdue to end; the depth says it has further to fall," the report said. On Nov. 22, the bear market was 412 days old, and earlier ones lasted 163 to 406 days from high to low, according to Galaxy.

Bitcoin was down 53% from its October 2025 record at that point. In past bear markets, it lost 77% to 93%. If the June low breaks, Galaxy sees possible new lows at about $48,500 and $28,200.

Galaxy tracks 13 bottom signals, and two of them have been met so far. According to the report, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETPs held about 1.24 million BTC, down 71,339 BTC since Oct. 4.

On Nov. 17, SkyBridge Capital founder Anthony Scaramucci asked Novogratz at the Digital Assets Forum in New York whether Bitcoin could return to $90,000 by the end of 2026. "Unlikely now," Novogratz said. "Less likely than it was. You need something to happen," he added.

#5114. Bitcoin Whales Accumulate $7.4 Billion in BTC, Breaking a Nine Year Pattern

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Bitcoin whales have reversed their usual year-end pattern. Between September 30 and November 21, balances in addresses holding 1,000 to 10,000 BTC rose by 121,117 BTC even though Bitcoin lost 29.5% of its value. At a reference price of $61,000, those additional coins are worth roughly $7.4 billion.

The figures come from CryptoQuant’s November 27 research report, which was supported by crypto lender CoinRabbit. The study excludes exchange and mining-pool addresses from its balance cohorts. Its findings are a snapshot through November 21, not a final tally for the quarter.

The timing matters. NewsBTC recently reported more than $2 billion in US spot Bitcoin ETF outflows. Fund withdrawals and rising whale balances point in different directions, but they measure different things. Neither tells us whether the same investors are moving their money from ETFs into direct Bitcoin ownership.

A broader measure from Maketo’s whale holdings data puts the balance of addresses with at least 1,000 BTC at 7.22 million BTC on November 26, up 54,379 BTC over the preceding 30 days. That group includes exchange and custody addresses, so it provides a separate view of where coins are held rather than an independent check of CryptoQuant’s 121,117 BTC figure.

The combined balance of the 1,000 to 10,000 BTC cohort at just under 2.95 million BTC on November 21, up from 2.83 million at the end of September.

Large addresses reduced their balances in seven of the nine preceding fourth quarters. Only 2019 and 2020 escaped that pattern. The 4.29% increase recorded so far this quarter is the largest Q4 gain since 2020, although December could still change the result.

For comparison, the cohort lost nearly 203,000 BTC over Q4 2025. This year’s increase has come during a falling market, rather than a rally.

There is a catch in calling this a $7.4 billion accumulation. The figure values the additional coins at a reference price; it does not measure the dollars spent buying them. Transfers between addresses, including movements across the cohort’s balance thresholds, can change the total without a market purchase.

The increase tells us where Bitcoin is sitting. It does not tell us how much fresh capital is behind it. That distinction matters when liquidity is scarce.

The 121,117 BTC figure makes for a bullish headline. The number I would pay closer attention to is the remaining profit margin.

Among addresses holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC, the unrealized profit margin fell from 33.9% at the end of September to 5.7% on November 21, its lowest reading of 2026 in the report.

The deterioration is even clearer in dollar terms. Combined unrealized profits for addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC stood at about $24 billion on November 21, down from a peak of $294 billion in August 2025.

Across the broader group of addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC, net realized losses reached approximately $2.1 billion in the first 52 days of Q4. The on-chain data suggests that some large holders are already moving coins at a loss rather than waiting for a recovery.

The relevant distinction is between the balance held at a given date and the profit or loss on coins that move. A growing balance does not prevent other coins within the cohort from being spent below their estimated cost basis.

Exchange deposits deserve a closer look, too. Inflows from unspent transaction outputs (UTXOs) of at least 1,000 BTC averaged 5,012 BTC per day in November through the report’s cutoff, compared with 3,239 in October. That is a measure of large coin outputs, not a count of individual whales.

November’s pickup should not obscure the bigger picture: the quarter-to-date average of 3,955 BTC per day remained below the 2019–2025 Q4 average of 4,575 BTC. Large deposits are not proof of sales, and a rise in this metric alone does not establish that selling pressure has intensified.

The 2018 and 2022 bear markets offer a useful comparison, though not a roadmap for this one.

Balances in the 1,000 to 10,000 BTC cohort declined in both of those fourth quarters. Their average unrealized profit margins were negative, while the group still had a positive margin at the November 21 reading this year.

Today’s accumulation may be a sign that some large holders are willing to retain exposure through the downturn. The address data cannot establish their motives or identify how much of the increase came from new purchases.

I would not call a market bottom on these numbers alone.

A further price decline could wipe out the cohort’s remaining profit cushion. Whether that produces more selling depends on the holders’ liquidity needs and positioning, neither of which can be read directly from address balances.

The next test is whether large-address balances keep rising while net realized losses and large exchange deposits ease. That combination, alongside evidence of renewed spot demand, would make the recovery case more convincing.

For now, the change in year-end positioning is real within CryptoQuant’s measured cohort. Evidence of a durable recovery is still missing.

#5113. ASEAN+3 announces new initiative to discuss digital asset regulations — Details

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Given the rise in the acceptance of digital assets, the ASEAN+3 member countries have agreed to establish a dedicated working group to advance discussions on cross-border digital payments and regulatory approaches to digital assets.

The decision was announced in the Co-chairs’ Statement following the ASEAN+3 Finance and Central Bank Deputies’ Meeting held in Kyoto, Japan recently.

Here, the initiative aims to strengthen regional financial cooperation by improving payment connectivity and encouraging discussions on how crypto should be regulated across participating economies.

In fact, it also marks a step towards greater coordination among Asian financial authorities as digital assets and blockchain-based financial services continue to expand.

To make this successful, the proposed working group aims to operate under the newly established AMRO Cross-Border Digital Payments Program. Under the same, they will provide a dedicated platform for ASEAN+3 economies to discuss retail and wholesale payment connectivity, alongside regulatory approaches to digital assets.

This is particularly important because cross-border payments remain fragmented across different financial systems. Needless to say, differences in payment infrastructure, regulations, and compliance requirements make international transactions slower and more expensive.

However, with greater coordination, participating economies could explore inter-operable payment systems and more consistent regulatory approaches.

Interestingly, the development also comes amid broader efforts by governments and financial regulators to address the growing influence of cryptocurrencies, stablecoins, and tokenized assets.

One prominent example is the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) framework. It became fully applicable on 30th December 2024, following the introduction of stablecoin-specific provisions in June 2024.

For those unaware, MiCA establishes common rules for crypto-asset issuers and service providers, covering authorization, transparency, investor protection, and market conduct. Its implementation has provided a regulatory benchmark for other jurisdictions considering comprehensive crypto frameworks.

South Africa is another example of this shift. In August 2026, the South African Reserve Bank (SARB) and National Treasury proposed an activity-based reporting framework for cross-border crypto transactions.

The proposal focuses on identifying and monitoring transactions that could facilitate capital flight, illegal financial flows, or regulatory circumvention. Rather than classifying crypto assets as official currency, it seeks to bring their cross-border movement under closer financial safeguards.

On the other hand, the United States has faced setbacks in establishing similar regulatory clarity. The proposed Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act failed to advance in the Senate on 15th September, receiving 49 votes in favor and 50 against. it was short of the 60 votes required to proceed.

Its failure has left the U.S without the proposed comprehensive federal market structure framework, potentially putting it behind jurisdictions such as the E.U in providing regulatory certainty. However, the SEC and CFTC continue to pursue regulatory initiatives under their existing authority.

Against this backdrop, ASEAN+3’s latest decision is the latest in the world’s global regulatory discussion/efforts.

Bitcoin whales have defied the negative trend seen in the Q4s of the past nine years as they have accumulated billions of dollars' worth of Bitcoin since Q4 2026 began.

Even though Bitcoin has faced severe price corrections during the period, with its price retesting levels not seen this year, Bitcoin whales have continued to buy the asset.

Onchain data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant shows that Bitcoin wallet addresses holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC have increased their holdings by 121,117 BTC in Q4 2026.

This defies the trend seen in the last nine Q4s, as Bitcoin whales have historically reduced their holdings during Q4 of each of the last nine years.

The source shared historic data from 2017, revealing that the Bitcoin whales recorded balance declines in seven of the last nine Q4 periods, with only 2019 and 2020 recording increases.

This means that the increase seen this month marks a major reversal of that historical trend, especially as Bitcoin has suffered even bigger price losses this Q4, dropping by about 29.5% over the same 52-day period.

Following the increase in Bitcoin whale accumulation seen in this quarter, further data shows that the whales now hold about 2.947 million BTC as of November 21, 2026.

Despite the increase in the holdings of Bitcoin whales this Q4, data also showed that these large holders have seen their unrealized profits drop significantly.

As such, unrealized profits among addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC have fallen to about $23.8 billion. Notably, this represents a massive decrease from the $124.7 billion recorded on September 30 and the record $294.4 billion in gains achieved on August 14, 2025.

#5111. Australia passes bill that would let people sue AI chatbot providers

The right to sue would start 12 months after Royal Assent and apply when a covered provider’s safety breach causes loss or damage.

Australia’s Parliament passed the Digital Duty of Care bill on Nov. 25, giving people a future route to sue covered AI chatbot providers over loss or damage caused by a breach of the new online safety duty. Both the duty and the right to sue are due to take effect 12 months after Royal Assent.

The Nov. 25 vote completed the bill’s passage through Parliament. Schedule 2 of Australia’s Digital Duty of Care bill sets out the safety duty and the private right of action. The Senate committee’s report sets out the transition period for that schedule. The communications department confirmed on Nov. 27 that the duty would start 12 months after Royal Assent.

A different part of the bill follows an earlier timetable. Schedule 1, including expanded powers for the eSafety Commissioner over apps and websites used to generate fake nude material, is due to take effect the day after Royal Assent.

Expanded eSafety powers start sooner than the digital duty and the court remedy.

The court remedy follows the 12-month timetable.

Calendar dates depend on when Royal Assent occurs. Branches show the sequence only.

Maps commencement rules for schedules 1 and 2 and the dated passage by Parliament. Connector lengths show sequence and branching.

Calendar dates depend on when Royal Assent occurs. Branches show the sequence only.

Section 28D covers providers of services that use an internet carriage service to generate material with AI. That brings covered AI chatbots within the scope of the private court remedy. The provision also names social media services, relevant electronic services and designated internet services.

Please enable JavaScript to verify and send this form.

A claimant would need to show that the provider failed to comply with its safety duty and that the failure caused their loss or damage. The bill treats that connection as established if the breach substantially contributed to the loss or damage.

The duty requires providers to take appropriate safety measures, including effective steps to address the risks they identify in their assessments. The explanatory memorandum, quoted by the Senate committee, says a harmful interaction does not necessarily establish a breach. The provider’s response to reasonably foreseeable risks matters, including whether it put effective safeguards in place and kept them working.

If a claim succeeds, the court could award damages, including for emotional distress, issue an injunction or order the provider to apologize. The bill gives courts discretion to choose a remedy suited to the circumstances.

The time limit for bringing a claim is tied to the claimant’s age and the date they suffered the loss or damage. Under section 28E, proceedings must begin before the later of their 21st birthday or six years after the day they suffered the loss or damage.

For someone who is already 21 when they suffer the loss, the six-year period gives the later date. For someone who suffers loss or damage as a child, the 21st birthday can be the later date, depending on their age when they suffered the loss.

#5109. Bitcoin Developer Warns Google Play Policy Could Lead to Home Invasions

On Nov. 27, Bitcoin developer Peter Todd warned that Google's plan to publicly display developers' addresses on the Play Store could lead to home invasions targeting developers of Bitcoin apps.

For independent developers working from home, the address displayed on Google Play could also be their residential address.

"There will be home invasions to compromise developers," Todd wrote on X.

He specifically highlighted the risks to developers of Bitcoin and other security-related apps, urging Google employees responsible for implementing the change to refuse to do so.

Starting March 1, 2027, Google Play will display the phone number and address of developers who use individual accounts to publish apps and identify themselves as traders.

Google explained that the requirement is related to its obligations as an online marketplace in the European Economic Area (EEA) and the UK.

The address and contact information will be visible to Play Store users worldwide.

The question is what address a developer might have to disclose, even for a relatively small app.

Dodemaide explained that Google support had informed him that he couldn't use a post office box because the address had to match his verified residential address.

He said he was considering removing his app from 31 countries to protect his home address.

Dodemaide also asked whether Google would allow individual developers to use a verified business mailing address instead.

Google lists several types of developers who may need to consider whether they qualify as traders, including those who sell apps, offer in-app purchases or earn advertising revenue.

For example, someone publishing an app purely as a hobby could declare themselves a non-trader.

Developers who don't distribute their apps in the EEA or UK are also considered non-traders under the policy.

Existing account holders have until Feb. 1, 2027, to submit their trader declarations, one month before the contact information becomes publicly visible.

Developers creating new accounts will need to make their declarations during account registration.

Google warns that failing to comply could prevent developers from updating their apps or result in their apps being removed from the Play Store globally.

The currency move cut the dollar cost of repaying unhedged yen loans. Monday’s two-year Japanese bond auction offers a fresh read on short-term yields.

The yen slipped against the dollar on Friday, cutting the dollar cost of repaying fixed, unhedged yen loans for traders who borrowed the currency to buy Bitcoin. Bitcoin held above 60,000 USDT on Binance during Tokyo trading as two measures of the city's November inflation moved in opposite directions. Monday's two-year government bond auction is the next chance to see whether the yen and short-term yields move higher together.

The Statistics Bureau of Japan said preliminary consumer prices across Tokyo's 23 wards rose 2.9% from a year earlier excluding fresh food, up from 2.6% in October. When energy is also excluded, inflation slowed to 2.5% from 2.6%. The preliminary Tokyo figures offer an early read ahead of the national release.

Electricity and city gas explain much of the split. Electricity prices rose 9.5% from a year earlier, up from 1.7% in October, and city gas prices rose 13.7%, up from 4.9%. Energy's contribution to the headline inflation rate increased by 0.34 percentage points. The overall rate rose more modestly, to 2.8% from 2.7%, as other categories offset part of that increase. The bureau put the increase in electricity's contribution at 0.22 percentage points, and city gas at 0.11.

Both Tokyo gauges were at 2.6% in October. In November the measure that includes energy rose, while the measure that excludes it slowed.

Electricity and city gas accounted for most of the increase in energy’s contribution to Tokyo’s headline inflation rate.

November values are preliminary and cover Tokyo’s 23 wards. Electricity and city gas are included in the energy total, and the printed contributions are rounded.

Ahead of the release, the risk for yen-funded Bitcoin trades was that hotter inflation could push the currency and short-term yields higher. An investor who borrows yen to buy Bitcoin and leaves the currency risk unhedged has to buy yen back to repay the loan. When the yen strengthens, the investor needs more dollars to repay the same yen balance even if Bitcoin's dollar price stands still. Friday's weaker yen moved that cost in the other direction.

Interest costs move on a different timetable. A trader pays more in interest if a yen loan has to be replaced at a higher rate. The actual rate and the timing depend on the instrument, maturity and any hedge, so traders with similar Bitcoin positions can face different costs.

Japan's Ministry of Finance has scheduled the November 30 two-year bond auction notice for 10:30 a.m. Tokyo time and the public result for 12:35 p.m. At October’s two-year auction, the yield at the weighted-average accepted price was 1.91%, giving traders a benchmark for the new issue.

The auction yield measures the return implied by the price paid for the new bonds. The two-year yield in secondary trading just before and after the result can show whether investors are repricing the path of Japanese rates. If that market yield rises while the yen strengthens against the dollar, borrowers who need to refinance could face dearer loans just as their outstanding yen debt becomes more expensive in dollars. If yields rise and the yen stays weak, the signals would still be split.

Even a move in both markets would leave open how many Bitcoin positions use yen funding. Bank for International Settlements researchers documented how hard it was to size the broader currency carry trade after the August 2024 unwind.

The XRP Ledger's native lending protocol entered a 14-day activation countdown on Friday after its amendments gained 29 of 35 validator votes, according to XRPScan. If support holds, the ledger will get native lending and borrowing as early as Dec. 11, for the first time since its launch in 2012.

Hussein Zangana, director of community at the XRP Ledger Foundation, cast the 29th vote with his validator and announced it in an X post on Friday. "I vote now for the Lending Protocol on the XRP Ledger and it's now in activation with 29 Yes votes," Zangana wrote.

𝗜 𝘃𝗼𝘁𝗲 𝗻𝗼𝘄 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗲 Lending Protocol 𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 XRP Ledger and it's now in activation with 29 Yes votes. 𝗩𝗲𝘁 𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗲𝘀📝: Lending and borrowing unlock capital and liquidity on the XRP Ledger, provide yield and make XRP and XRPL assets usable as collateral. I appreciate the efforts exercised by the community to give this amendment a good screening! For validators this is important assistance and help in making educated decisions. Let's dive into why i voted Yes for Lending on XRP🧵.

According to XRPScan, LendingProtocol and its update LendingProtocolV1_1 both reached 29 votes on Friday. The earliest activation date for LendingProtocolV1_1 is Dec. 11, and its support has to stay above 80% until then. SingleAssetVault, the third amendment in the package, has 30 votes and can activate as early as Dec. 9.

"Lending and borrowing unlock capital and liquidity on the XRP Ledger, provide yield and make XRP and XRPL assets usable as collateral," Zangana added in the same post.

Ripple engineer Vito Tumas first proposed the protocol in April 2024. According to the XLS-65 standard, each Single Asset Vault holds only one asset, such as XRP or RLUSD, and depositors get vault shares in the form of Multi-Purpose Tokens.

Under XLS-66, a loan broker uses that capital to issue loans with a fixed term and a fixed rate. The broker checks borrowers off-chain and can post its own first-loss capital to cover defaults. Interest payments go back into the vault, and the protocol has no on-chain liquidations.

"Represent value. Move value. Trade value. Now: finance value," Jazzi Cooper, head of product at RippleX, wrote on X about the vote. According to Cooper, the team made "deliberate design decisions: protocol native, built-in compliance, and off-chain underwriting."

J. Ayo Akinyele, head of engineering at RippleX, wrote that the vaults and the protocol went through "multiple independent audits, a public Attackathon, formal verification, AI-assisted reviews, community testing, and validator review." Ripple and Common Prefix did the formal verification in the Lean 4 theorem prover. "Traditional testing isn't enough when you're building DeFi directly into Layer-1," Tumas wrote.

Clearpool said that it would bring "real-world, institutional-ready lending infrastructure, built natively on XRPL." The platform plans a credit fund on the ledger with Ripple and Cicada Partners, and it has already tested a full loan cycle on Devnet. "We want to make real loans to real businesses," Tom Lombardi of Cicada Partners said.

Evernorth CEO Ashish Birla said that his company "is exploring how XLS-66 could support yield generation as part of our broader treasury strategy."

According to XRPScan, SingleAssetVault can go live on Dec. 9, and the two lending amendments can follow on Dec. 11 if their support holds.

#5105. 11-year Ethereum whale cashes out — What does it say about ETH’s price bottom?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Dormant sell-offs in a bear market can send two very different signals.

It may suggest that long-term holders have waning belief in an asset. Alternatively, it may just be an example of investors realizing profits having owned something for a long period of time. If the market interprets the sale as an indication that the market is nearing its bottom, FOMO might be in store.

Interestingly, a recent Ethereum whale’s move has brought this debate back into focus. The whale bought 100,000 ETH for just $31,000 in 2015. It has now sold its final 45,000 ETH for $75.3 million. In total, the investment generated over $87 million, translating to nearly 2,800x returns.

Naturally, the question is whether this was simply profit-taking.

Technically, Ethereum has fallen by 40%+ in 2026, bringing it down to currently around $1.7K. This is almost 65% less than the all-time high for ETH of $4.9K in 2025. This puts the whales’ last 45,000 ETH sell-off at an average of around $1,673, again similar to current prices, but well off cycle highs. Therefore, despite having enjoyed huge overall profits, the whale elected to sell in a deep market downturn, not in a rising market.

Could this be a whale securing profits, or is it a loss of confidence in Ethereum’s [ETH] recovery? With the price still deep below its cycle high, the dormant whale may have further motives behind the selling.

Usually, when dormant whales sell into market weakness, it raises the question of whether they see further downside that the broader market is yet to price in.

Technically, a 30% correction would also take ETH back towards its 2023 lows. A pivotal support area exists at $1.5K and should this be breached, further downside may follow. Especially given that bearishness has been on the rise. Indeed, the warning signs have been showing up in market data too.

Ethereum ETFs recorded $523.3 million in net outflows across eight trading sessions through 25th November. ETH has continued to underperform Bitcoin too. The broader altcoin market is also taking a hit. In fact, not a single one of the top-50 altcoins is up since Q4 began, while the median altcoin has lost 40% of its value in less than two months.

This points to weak capital inflows and limited risk appetite, making an Ethereum recovery harder to sustain.

Against this backdrop, the whale’s exit looks less like routine profit-taking and more like fading confidence in ETH’s recovery. This is important because whale selling near market bottoms can sometimes signal a buying opportunity. However, weak inflows and bearish market conditions make that case harder to support.

Thus, Ethereum’s weakness appears to be reaching even long-dormant wallets, adding further pressure to its bottoming thesis.

An 11-year-old Ethereum whale sold its final 45,000 ETH, raising questions about investor confidence.

Weak ETF inflows, falling altcoins, and ETH’s price decline put its recovery and $1.5K support at risk.

#5103. Google’s lightweight Gemini matched two top models on a chemistry test

All three identified known compounds in about 97% of attempts when given the same chemistry tools and web access.

Google DeepMind released tools for interpreting mass spectrometry data in its Antigravity AI platform on Nov. 25. In the company’s test, the software helped its lightweight Gemini 3.8 Flash match two frontier models at identifying known compounds. With the tools and internet access, all three identified the exact molecule in about 97% of attempts on a set of 100 compounds whose fragment patterns were already recorded in public libraries.

The models were farther apart with internet access alone. In DeepMind’s benchmark, Flash missed more than three quarters of its attempts to identify a compound, while Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 4 Carbon missed roughly a quarter to a third. All three scored below 4% with neither internet access nor the specialist tools.

DeepMind drew the test spectra from the Enamine REAL collection in the public MoNA library. The compounds’ structures were also cataloged in PubChem. The team screened out recordings in which the molecule had produced too few useful fragments. The benchmark ran three attempts per spectrum. Runs that took more than an hour counted as failures, while temporary infrastructure and quota errors were excluded.

Tandem mass spectrometry measures the charged fragments a molecule breaks into. To identify the molecule, a chemist can compare that pattern with a reference spectrum recorded from a known compound.

For the internet-only runs, DeepMind said scripts written on the fly struggled with noisy peaks and with choosing which masses to search. The new Mass Spec Skills give Antigravity established software to clean up a signal, look for matching reference spectra and check whether a proposed structure fits the measured fragments.

DeepMind also reported that adding the skills reduced the number of tokens each model generated per attempt, with the largest proportional drop for Flash. Flash with the tools was more accurate than either frontier model with internet access alone.

DeepMind tested 100 compounds with internet access and Mass Spec Skills. In a separate demonstration with library lookup disabled, it recovered a compound already cataloged in PubChem.

In a test without a spectral-library search, Antigravity used fragment measurements to infer a formula and narrow down candidate structures in PubChem. The compound it selected was already cataloged.

For a compound that is genuinely new, a predicted formula and explanations for some of the peaks can give a chemist a starting point. DeepMind says some structures, including mirror-image molecules, break apart in such similar ways that telling them apart can take another kind of lab measurement.

#5102. ‘Give It Up’: Saylor Fires Back at Infamous Bitcoin Critic

When American entrepreneur Jeffrey Tucker told Bitcoiners to stop dreaming about Bitcoin becoming the world's most valuable asset, Strategy co-founder Michael Saylor responded with the example of a gold-backed banknote.

"Give it up, Bitcoiners. There is no such thing as money that is not used in exchange," Tucker wrote on X.

Tucker argued that Bitcoiners had brought the criticism upon themselves. They made the mistake of thinking they could simply declare Bitcoin a store of value and that would somehow make it one. That is not how it works, according to Tucker. He argued that nothing in the history of money supports this idea.

In his response, Saylor started with an example involving a bakery. Suppose someone buys bread at a bakery. They pay for the bread with a gold-backed banknote. The baker can use that banknote to pay the miller.  The miller can use it to pay the farmer. All three transactions could be completed using the same banknote, while the gold stays in the vault.

@jeffreytucker Jeffrey, a gold-backed banknote could pay the baker, the miller, and the farmer while the gold stayed in the vault. Today people pay in dollars and save in gold, stocks, and real estate. Bitcoin is competing for those savings.

In the second part of his response, Saylor made an argument familiar to anyone who gets paid in dollars.

Sure, you can use dollars to buy groceries. However, you can still decide to keep some of your wealth in stocks, gold, or real estate.

"Today people pay in dollars and save in gold, stocks, and real estate. Bitcoin is competing for those savings," Saylor wrote.

This last point was less ambitious than the claim Tucker was pushing back against.

Tucker was talking about Bitcoin becoming the world's most valuable asset.

Saylor, meanwhile, was making a simpler argument about where people choose to keep their savings.

However, Saylor's gold analogy raises an interesting question for Tucker. In Saylor's example, gold is still relevant to the purchase of bread because it backs the banknote the baker accepts.

However, in his modern examples, someone who chooses to save in stocks isn't necessarily concerned about whether their local bakery accepts stocks as payment.

For Tucker, it's all about how the customer pays for a loaf of bread. For Saylor, it's about what the baker does with the money after selling it.

#5098. ‘Not your Silicon, not your keys’ — Ethereum’s Buterin calls for open-source chip design

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has come up with an amendment to crypto’s oldest security motto, arguing that key safety increasingly depends on open-source chip designs.

In a blog post titled A shallow dive into open-source chip design, published on 26th November, Buterin shed light on the importance of making hardware designs publicly accessible and verifiable. He also argued that while the crypto industry has focused on securing software, cryptographic protocols, and private keys, underlying hardware remains an overlooked security risk.

Even if wallet software is secure, compromised hardware could expose sensitive information, including private keys and seed phrases.

Given the case in point, Buterin believes that verifying how a computer operates ultimately requires examining its underlying hardware, including transistors, silicon, and electrical circuits.

Even when software is open-source and independently audited, users have limited visibility into what the underlying chip actually does.

Probably the most frustrating thing about chip design is how opaque and proprietary the whole thing is.

To explain this risk better, he took reference from an attack involving a malicious implant with an eSIM inserted into a hardware wallet before it reaches consumers. Once activated, the implant can exfiltrate the wallet’s seed phrase.

Using this example, he also warned that attackers could replace legitimate chips with nearly identical versions containing additional malicious features. These, in turn, could bypass software-level security checks.

Not only this, but Buterin also believes that publicly accessible hardware designs would allow independent researchers to verify whether chips perform their intended functions.

However, publishing a chip’s Verilog code alone is insufficient. He argued that meaningful verification requires openness down to the GDS level, which describes the actual physical geometry of a chip’s components.

He also highlighted Process Design Kits (PDKs), which contain manufacturing-specific information and design rules needed to produce and validate chips.

Buterin highlighted IRIS, a chip-inspection technique being developed by hardware researcher Bunnie, which uses optical imaging to examine chip structures.

More sophisticated attacks involving changes to doping levels may require destructive methods such as Focused Ion Beam-Scanning Electron Microscopy (FIB-SEM).

He also proposed designing chips for easier inspection by enabling independent testing of smaller components, reducing dependence on fragile configurations, and making physical layouts more inspection-friendly.

Rather than expecting consumers to inspect chips themselves, he envisions professional auditors, journalists, and civil society groups using specialized equipment to verify manufacturers’ claims.

Finally, Buterin acknowledged that performance-intensive sectors such as AI are unlikely to adopt open-source manufacturing entirely. Instead, he is expecting a divide between performance-focused and security-focused hardware, with the latter prioritizing transparency and verifiability over efficiency.

He concluded it best by extending crypto’s familiar motto, “not your keys, not your coins”, with a hardware-focused warning.
